This chemical glyco-modification is performed entirely post-isolation, preserves EV membrane integrity under the mild reaction conditions, and exploits a state-specific receptor axis that is activated across diverse cell types during damage.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose installing di-α2,8-linked sialic acid motifs on the surface of isolated EVs via post-isolation sialyltransferase treatment to engage Siglec-E (murine) and its human orthologs Siglec-7 and Siglec-9, which are upregulated on myeloid cells under inflammatory conditions. Isolated EVs will first be treated with neuraminidase to strip heterogeneous sialylation, then with recombinant α2,8-sialyltransferase (ST8Sia) and CMP-Neu5Ac to build defined α2,8-linked disialic acid structures on exposed galactose acceptors. These engineered EVs will be loaded with dexamethasone or resolvin D1 lipid mediator and evaluated for preferential binding to and anti-inflammatory signaling through Siglec receptors on LPS-activated versus resting macrophages and neutrophils. Efficacy will be tested in murine cecal ligation and puncture sepsis and intratracheal LPS-induced ARDS models, measuring inflammatory cytokine reduction, organ damage scores, and survival. This approach differs from prior sialic acid nanoparticle work by exploiting the biological EV chassis and achieving glycan installation through enzymatic remodeling rather than synthetic polymer chemistry, preserving the native biocompatibility and signaling capability of EVs.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a post-isolation strategy that combines partial desialylation with fucosyltransferase-mediated modification to generate Lewis X epitopes on EV surfaces, targeting Dendritic Cell-Specific ICAM-Grabbing Nonintegrin (DC-SIGN) and related C-type lectins upregulated on inflammatory dendritic cells and macrophages at damage sites. EVs isolated from mesenchymal stromal cells will be treated with a controlled dose of Arthrobacter ureafaciens sialidase to expose terminal galactose, followed by incubation with recombinant α1,3-fucosyltransferase VI and GDP-fucose to install Lewis X trisaccharide motifs. The modified EVs, loaded with TGF-β mRNA, will be assessed for selective uptake by monocyte-derived dendritic cells stimulated with inflammatory cytokines versus immature dendritic cells in vitro. In vivo, a dextran sodium sulfate colitis model will test whether Lewis X–EVs preferentially accumulate in inflamed colonic lamina propria and attenuate disease activity index, histological score, and pro-inflammatory gene expression. This exogenous two-step glycan editing pipeline is entirely cell-free and exploits inflammation-associated lectin upregulation without restricting targeting to a single cell lineage.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering isolated EVs to display β-glucosylceramide (β-GlcCer) glycolipid motifs on their outer leaflet to engage the macrophage-inducible C-type lectin Mincle (CLEC4E), which is strongly upregulated on myeloid cells during sterile inflammation and tissue damage. β-GlcCer–lipid conjugates will be synthesized with a membrane-anchoring alkyl chain and inserted into pre-isolated EV membranes by brief sonication-mediated membrane fusion, a mild post-isolation approach preserving vesicle topology and cargo integrity. The resulting Mincle-targeted EVs, loaded with anti-inflammatory peptides or IL-4 mRNA, will be tested for preferential uptake by LPS-primed bone-marrow-derived macrophages versus resting macrophages, with Mincle-knockout cells as a specificity control. In vivo validation will employ a sterile peritonitis model induced by monosodium urate crystals, where Mincle expression is dramatically induced; biodistribution will be tracked by bioluminescence and therapeutic benefit assessed by peritoneal leukocyte count and cytokine profiling. This platform uniquely couples a glycolipid-insertion approach with a damage-induced lectin target that is not constitutively expressed, ensuring state-selective rather than lineage-selective delivery.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a dual-glycan strategy in which isolated EVs are simultaneously decorated with desialylated O-glycan structures (exposed Thomsen-Friedenreich antigen, Galβ1-3GalNAc) and terminal N-acetylglucosamine residues, to target galectin-3 lattices and the GlcNAc-binding intelectin-1, both of which accumulate on the surface of cells under inflammatory and hypoxic stress. Post-isolation, EV glycans will be sequentially remodeled: neuraminidase treatment will unmask T antigen on O-glycans, while specific galactosidase followed by recombinant GlcNAc-transferase will install terminal GlcNAc on N-glycan branches. This combinatorial glycan display is hypothesized to achieve synergistic binding avidity specifically in the inflamed microenvironment where both lectins are co-expressed. EVs loaded with antioxidant enzyme catalase or SOD mRNA will be tested in ischemia-reperfusion injury models of the kidney, comparing accumulation in injured versus contralateral kidneys. This dual-targeting glycoengineered EV platform is unprecedented in its simultaneous exploitation of two damage-upregulated lectin systems through purely exogenous enzymatic remodeling.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose constructing a glycan-based inflammation-sensing EV platform by conjugating synthetic mannose-6-phosphate (M6P) glycan ligands to the surface of isolated EVs, targeting the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor (CI-MPR) that is redistributed to the cell surface of damaged, stressed, or senescent cells. Under homeostatic conditions CI-MPR primarily cycles between the trans-Golgi and endosomes, but oxidative stress, DNA damage, and senescence cause its aberrant surface accumulation. Isolated EVs will undergo chemoenzymatic glycan remodeling: endoglycosidase digestion to the core GlcNAc followed by transglycosylation with a synthetic M6P-tetrasaccharide oxazoline using an EndoA glycosynthase mutant. The M6P-displaying EVs, loaded with senolytic prodrug or autophagy-inducing peptide cargo, will be evaluated for selective uptake by etoposide-induced senescent versus proliferating fibroblasts and endothelial cells. In vivo, efficacy will be assessed in aged mice or bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, monitoring clearance of senescent cells and reduction of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype. This approach repurposes an established chemoenzymatic platform for EV surface remodeling and exploits a damage-state–specific receptor trafficking event rather than cell-type identity.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose the computational design of de novo miniproteins that function as synthetic autophagy receptors to selectively clear disease-associated protein aggregates, such as mutant huntingtin or TDP-43 inclusions, from the cytoplasm. Using RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN, bifunctional proteins will be generated bearing one face that binds aggregate-specific epitopes (exposed hydrophobic patches or polyglutamine stretches) and an opposing face that engages LC3/GABARAP on autophagosomal membranes via a computationally optimized LIR-mimicking surface. Unlike antibody-fusion AceTACs, these fully de novo constructs will be small enough for mRNA-based delivery, will avoid the immunogenicity of antibody fragments, and can be tuned for aggregate-selectivity versus monomer-sparing by exploiting avidity differences. Delivered as LNP-encapsulated mRNA to the CNS, the expressed miniproteins would transiently bridge toxic aggregates to the autophagy machinery without broadly perturbing proteostasis. The approach addresses a critical gap where small-molecule degraders lack the large interface recognition needed to distinguish pathological assemblies from functional monomers, offering a protein-scale solution to aggregate clearance in neurodegeneration.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to design de novo protein tethers that restore deficient mitochondria-ER membrane contact sites in cells harboring disease-associated mutations in endogenous tethering complexes such as VAPB-PTPIP51, whose loss is implicated in ALS and frontotemporal dementia. Using RFdiffusion, we will computationally generate compact single-chain proteins with two orthogonal membrane-anchoring modules: one targeting the outer mitochondrial membrane via a designed TOM20-binding or lipid-inserting domain, and one targeting the ER via interaction with SEC61 or reticulon family proteins. Protein geometry will be tuned to enforce a 10-30 nm inter-organelle gap optimal for calcium and lipid transfer. Unlike overexpression of native tethers, which risks stoichiometric imbalance and dominant-negative effects, these designed tethers are engineered for defined valency, controlled expression from mRNA, and minimal perturbation to endogenous complexes. Functional rescue will be assessed by measuring ER-to-mitochondria calcium flux and cardiolipin restoration in patient-derived motor neurons. This approach addresses a pathogenic mechanism inaccessible to small molecules and antibodies alike, leveraging protein-scale spatial precision to correct organelle topology.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to design de novo intracellular scaffold proteins that rewire oncogenic MAPK signaling by competitively sequestering pathway kinases into non-productive complexes. Using computational design, we will generate multivalent scaffolds presenting orthogonal binding surfaces for RAF and MEK that mimic the geometry of native KSR1 scaffold contacts but deliberately exclude ERK-docking motifs. Expressed intracellularly via mRNA, these designed scaffolds would create kinase-sequestering sinks that attenuate pathway output in a graded, tunable manner without requiring catalytic inhibition. This approach circumvents the paradoxical pathway activation and feedback rebound that plague RAF kinase inhibitors. The protein-scale advantage lies in the ability to recognize multiple flat protein-protein interfaces simultaneously, something unachievable with small molecules. Design candidates will be validated in BRAF-V600E melanoma cells by measuring dose-dependent suppression of ERK phosphorylation and proliferation without paradoxical MAPK activation. This scaffold-based signaling interception represents a distinct modality from receptor agonism or antagonism, operating entirely within the cytoplasm to impose a new topology on a disease-driving signaling cascade.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to computationally design de novo proteins that selectively dissolve or prevent the maturation of pathological stress granules while sparing physiological granule cycling. The designed proteins will target the NTF2-like domain of G3BP1, a central nucleator of stress granules whose aberrant persistence is linked to ALS and cancer chemoresistance. Using RFdiffusion, we will generate miniprotein binders that engage the G3BP1 NTF2 domain at a site overlapping its dimerization interface, thereby raising the local concentration threshold for phase separation without fully ablating transient stress responses. Unlike small-molecule covalent modifiers of G3BP1, which alter charge and risk off-target reactivity, de novo protein binders offer reversible, high-specificity engagement of the shallow NTF2 surface. The designed proteins will be expressed from mRNA and validated by live-cell imaging of stress granule dynamics, measuring granule persistence time and composition under arsenite stress. This condensate-modulating strategy addresses a pathological process that is currently undruggable by conventional modalities, exploiting protein-scale interface recognition to fine-tune phase behavior rather than abolish it entirely.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to design de novo allosteric protein switches that sense pathological intracellular metabolites and conditionally activate a therapeutic output only in diseased cells. Specifically, we will engineer a single-chain protein that undergoes a conformational change upon binding oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate, which accumulates in IDH1/2-mutant gliomas and AML. The conformational switch will be designed to expose a cryptic degron or E3 ligase-recruiting surface only in the metabolite-bound state, enabling conditional degradation of a disease-relevant target such as HIF2α. Using RFdiffusion2 for ligand-binding pocket design and computational insertion of allosteric coupling elements, this autonomous sense-and-respond protein would function without external control. This conditional logic addresses the major limitation of constitutively active degraders—namely systemic toxicity from on-target degradation in healthy tissues. The approach leverages protein-scale advantages in building multi-domain sense-response architectures inaccessible to small-molecule PROTACs. Designs will be validated in isogenic IDH-mutant and wild-type cell lines, measuring metabolite-dependent target degradation and selectivity windows.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to design de novo proteins that redirect the subcellular localization of oncogenic transcription factors by creating synthetic nuclear export adaptors. Targeting MYC, which is considered undruggable by small molecules due to its intrinsically disordered nature and lack of binding pockets, we will design a protein comprising an RFdiffusion-generated binder for the MYC bHLH-ZIP dimerization domain fused to computationally optimized, CRM1-recognized nuclear export signals. Expressed intracellularly, this adaptor would forcibly relocalize MYC to the cytoplasm, separating it from chromatin and abrogating its transcriptional program without requiring direct inhibition of its protein-protein interactions with MAX. The protein-scale advantage is twofold: the designed binder can engage MYC's large, flat dimerization surface, and the export signal can be presented at precisely controlled stoichiometry. Functional validation will use MYC-dependent lymphoma cell lines, measuring nuclear MYC depletion by fractionation, suppression of MYC target gene signatures, and anti-proliferative effects. This relocalization strategy represents a modality mechanistically distinct from degradation or binding-based inhibition.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to computationally design de novo bifunctional proteins that act as genetically encoded protein-level PROTACs, bridging undruggable intracellular targets to underexplored E3 ubiquitin ligases for selective proteasomal degradation. While recent work has demonstrated proof-of-concept for de novo designed protein degraders using BCL-xL and KLHL20, we will systematically expand the accessible E3 ligase repertoire by designing binders for tissue-restricted ligases such as KLHL40 in muscle or TRIM9 in neurons, enabling cell-type-selective degradation. Using RFdiffusion to generate target-binding and ligase-recruiting surfaces on a single compact scaffold, and ProteinMPNN for sequence optimization, these bioPROTACs overcome fundamental limitations of small-molecule PROTACs: namely, their restriction to four canonical E3 ligases and poor ternary complex control for undruggable targets with flat surfaces. Delivered as mRNA, the designed proteins achieve transient, dose-controllable degradation. Validation will be performed by targeting oncogenic KRAS-G12D in pancreatic cancer cells using neuron- or muscle-restricted E3 ligases as negative controls for tissue selectivity, assessing degradation efficiency, selectivity over wild-type KRAS, and downstream pathway suppression.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to design de novo protein cages that function as synthetic organelles for metabolic rescue in inborn errors of metabolism. Using computationally designed self-assembling protein nanocages with engineered interior surfaces, we will encapsulate therapeutic enzyme cargo—such as phenylalanine hydroxylase for phenylketonuria—within a porous protein shell that permits substrate and product diffusion while protecting the enzyme from proteolytic degradation and immune surveillance. The nanocage interior will be functionalized with computationally designed binding motifs that recruit and orient the enzyme, and pore geometry will be tuned to exclude large proteases while admitting small-molecule substrates. Expressed from mRNA or delivered as purified protein with cell-penetrating moieties, these synthetic organelles would provide sustained intracellular enzymatic activity in hepatocytes. This approach addresses the fundamental limitation of enzyme replacement therapy—rapid intracellular degradation and immunogenicity of naked enzymes—while avoiding the irreversibility and insertional mutagenesis risks of gene therapy. Designs will be validated by measuring phenylalanine clearance rates in patient-derived hepatocytes and enzyme half-life extension within cages.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to design de novo proteins that act as synthetic signaling adaptors capable of rewiring the integrated stress response from a maladaptive pro-apoptotic output toward a pro-survival translational program in cardiomyocytes during ischemia-reperfusion injury. The designed protein will contain a computationally generated binding surface for the DELE1 C-terminal domain that blocks its interaction with HRI kinase, coupled to a second surface that recruits GADD34 phosphatase to eIF2α, thereby accelerating translational recovery. This dual-function protein intervenes at two nodes of the ISR simultaneously—something impossible for a single small molecule—to reshape the signaling outcome from stress-induced apoptosis toward adaptive proteostasis. Expressed from modified mRNA delivered via cardiac-targeted lipid nanoparticles, the designed adaptor would act transiently during the critical reperfusion window. Validation will include measurement of eIF2α phosphorylation dynamics, ATF4 target gene expression, and cardiomyocyte survival in ex vivo heart ischemia-reperfusion models. This pathway-rewiring approach addresses a clinical need unmet by existing kinase inhibitors, which lack the multispecific, intracellular, node-bridging capacity of a designed protein.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to design de novo proteins that selectively nucleate or dissolve specific nuclear condensates to reprogram transcriptional states in cancer. Specifically, we will target super-enhancer condensates driven by the intrinsically disordered regions of BRD4 and MED1, whose aberrant coalescence sustains oncogene expression in multiple myeloma and other cancers. Using computational design, we will generate multivalent miniproteins displaying aromatic and charged residue patterns calibrated to act as competitive co-condensation partners that dilute the effective valency of BRD4 IDR interactions, raising the critical concentration for condensate formation and thereby selectively collapsing oncogenic super-enhancer condensates. Unlike BET-bromodomain inhibitors, which broadly displace BRD4 from acetylated histones, these condensate-disrupting proteins would specifically target the phase-separation-dependent fraction of BRD4 function, potentially offering greater selectivity and reduced toxicity. Delivered via mRNA, designs will be validated by quantifying super-enhancer condensate number and MYC transcriptional output in myeloma cells, along with global transcriptional profiling to assess specificity of condensate dissolution.

label: claude_opus_46
text: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is fundamentally a length-dependent axonopathy in which distal nerve fibers degenerate progressively, yet the molecular programs governing this degeneration in specific DRG neuron subtypes remain poorly resolved. We propose using scRNA-seq on DRGs harvested from transgenic diabetic mouse models (db/db and high-fat diet/STZ) at early, intermediate, and late neuropathy stages to construct a temporally resolved, subtype-specific transcriptomic atlas of DRG neuronal responses to metabolic stress. By computationally identifying subtype-selective vulnerability genes and dysregulated signaling modules, we will nominate candidate therapeutic targets in the most affected neuronal populations, such as nonpeptidergic nociceptors. Lead targets will be functionally validated using an organ-on-a-chip platform reconstituting iPSC-derived sensory neurons under diabetic-milieu conditions, enabling real-time electrophysiological and axonal integrity readouts. This integrated approach will reveal which DRG neuron subtypes are most therapeutically tractable and yield novel subtype-selective drug targets for disease-modifying intervention in diabetic neuropathy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: Recent work has identified the SIRT3–SARM1 axis as a critical mediator of hyperglycemia-induced axonal NAD+ depletion and degeneration in diabetic peripheral neuropathy, and pyruvate kinase M has been shown to physically activate SARM1 under high-glucose conditions. We propose to develop and screen peptide and small-molecule disruptors of the PKM–SARM1 protein-protein interaction using structure-guided design informed by AlphaFold modeling and to test them in a diabetic neuropathy organ-on-a-chip system comprising iPSC-derived DRG sensory neurons exposed to hyperglycemic and dyslipidemic conditions. Lead compounds will be validated in streptozotocin-induced and high-fat-diet transgenic diabetic mouse models, assessing axonal NAD+ levels, intraepidermal nerve fiber density, nerve conduction velocity, and pain behavior. This strategy advances beyond broad NAD+ supplementation or global SARM1 catalytic inhibition by selectively targeting a disease-potentiated protein interface, potentially offering a safer and more specific neuroprotective therapeutic approach for diabetic patients.

label: claude_opus_46
text: Endoneurial microvascular dysfunction, characterized by pericyte degeneration, basement membrane thickening, and endothelial NO signaling impairment, is an early event in diabetic neuropathy that precedes detectable axonal loss. We propose to build a vascularized nerve-on-a-chip platform incorporating human iPSC-derived endothelial cells, pericytes, and sensory neurons in a perfusable microfluidic architecture that recapitulates the vasa nervorum microenvironment under diabetic metabolic stress. Using this system, we will perform scRNA-seq on endothelial and pericyte compartments to identify hyperglycemia-driven transcriptomic programs that impair neurovascular coupling and endoneurial perfusion. Candidate pathways, such as AGE-RAGE-mediated pericyte apoptosis and PKC-dependent eNOS uncoupling, will be targeted pharmacologically and validated in diabetic transgenic mice using intravital imaging of sciatic nerve vasculature and concurrent nerve function assessments. This neurovascular-focused strategy addresses a critical but therapeutically underexploited compartment in diabetic neuropathy pathogenesis.

label: claude_opus_46
text: Satellite glial cells in the DRG transfer mitochondria to sensory neurons via MYO10-dependent tunneling nanotubes, and this process is profoundly impaired in diabetic neuropathy due to reduced MYO10 expression. We propose to develop gene therapy and pharmacological strategies that restore or enhance SGC-to-neuron mitochondrial transfer as a neuroprotective intervention. Specifically, we will design AAV vectors with SGC-selective promoters to overexpress MYO10 or Miro1 in satellite glia of diabetic transgenic mice and assess whether enhanced mitochondrial donation rescues neuronal bioenergetics, prevents axonal degeneration, and alleviates neuropathic pain. In parallel, we will use scRNA-seq of diabetic DRGs to map the metabolic and transcriptional alterations in SGC subpopulations that underlie impaired tunneling nanotube formation and identify druggable upstream regulators of MYO10 downregulation. This approach targets the neuron-glia metabolic unit rather than the neuron or glial cell alone, representing a mechanistically distinct therapeutic paradigm for diabetic neuropathy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: Diabetic neuropathy is accompanied by persistent pro-inflammatory macrophage infiltration into peripheral nerves, and recent evidence indicates that diabetic macrophages exhibit metabolic inflexibility that prevents their transition from the M1 to the reparative M2 phenotype. We propose to dissect the endoneurial macrophage metabolic reprogramming that stalls M1-to-M2 polarization using scRNA-seq on macrophages isolated from sciatic nerves and DRGs of high-fat-diet and db/db diabetic mice at progressive neuropathy stages. Key metabolic checkpoints, including impaired PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling, GLUT1 downregulation, and simultaneous glycolytic and oxidative phosphorylation failure, will be targeted with metabolic reprogramming agents such as dimethyl fumarate or itaconate derivatives delivered via nanoparticle formulations with endoneurial tropism. Therapeutic efficacy will be evaluated in diabetic transgenic mice by measuring macrophage phenotype switching, nerve conduction velocity, intraepidermal nerve fiber density, and pain behavior. This immune-metabolic strategy addresses a fundamental barrier to endogenous nerve repair in diabetic neuropathy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: Hyperglycemia-induced epigenetic modifications in DRG neurons, including aberrant histone methylation by the methyltransferase G9a and altered DNA methylation patterns, have been implicated in the persistent downregulation of potassium channel genes and the maintenance of neuronal hyperexcitability underlying painful diabetic neuropathy. We propose to perform integrated single-cell multi-omics profiling, combining snRNA-seq with single-cell ATAC-seq, on DRG neurons from diabetic transgenic mice and postmortem human DRGs to construct a comprehensive epigenomic landscape of diabetes-driven chromatin remodeling in sensory neuron subtypes. Based on the identified epigenetic drivers, we will test targeted epigenetic therapies, including G9a inhibitors and HDAC modulators, for their ability to restore K+ channel expression and normalize neuronal excitability using DRG neuron cultures on an organ-on-a-chip electrophysiology platform. Lead epigenetic interventions will be validated in vivo for reversal of mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia, offering a precision epigenetic medicine approach to painful diabetic neuropathy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: Gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites, including reduced short-chain fatty acids and elevated trimethylamine-N-oxide, have been causally implicated in diabetic neuropathy through Mendelian randomization and preclinical studies, yet the molecular mechanisms linking circulating microbial metabolites to DRG neuron and vasa nervorum injury remain unclear. We propose to combine fecal microbiome shotgun sequencing with plasma metabolomics and DRG scRNA-seq in a high-fat-diet transgenic mouse model of diabetic neuropathy, with and without fecal microbiota transplantation from healthy donors or defined consortia of protective bacterial species. This systems-level approach will identify specific metabolite-receptor axes, such as SCFA signaling via free fatty acid receptors on DRG neurons and endothelial cells, that mediate neuroprotection or neurotoxicity. Candidate metabolite-receptor interactions will be validated in a neurovascular organ-on-a-chip platform, establishing mechanistic links between the gut-nerve axis and informing microbiome-directed therapies for diabetic neuropathy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: Neuronal pyroptosis driven by NLRP3 inflammasome activation in DRG neurons has emerged as a contributor to sensory neuron death and neuropathic pain in diabetic neuropathy, and GLP-1 receptor agonists have shown preliminary neuroprotective effects by suppressing this pathway. We propose to systematically characterize the cell-type-specific activation of canonical and non-canonical pyroptosis pathways in DRG neurons, resident macrophages, and satellite glial cells of diabetic transgenic mice using multiplexed spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence at progressive disease stages. Building on this characterization, we will develop and test DRG-targeted nanoparticle delivery of selective GSDMD inhibitors or NLRP3-specific antagonists such as MCC950, comparing their neuroprotective efficacy to systemic GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment. Outcomes including neuronal survival, inflammasome activation markers, nerve fiber density, and pain behavior will be assessed, providing a mechanistic rationale for combining anti-pyroptotic therapy with metabolic interventions as a multimodal treatment strategy for diabetic neuropathy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: The concept of hyperglycemic memory posits that diabetes-induced nerve damage persists even after glycemic normalization, implicating stable epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming of the endoneurial vasculature and DRG neurons. We propose to model hyperglycemic memory in diabetic transgenic mice by restoring euglycemia with insulin after an initial hyperglycemic period and performing longitudinal scRNA-seq on DRG neurons, endoneurial endothelial cells, and immune cells to identify gene regulatory networks that remain aberrantly activated despite metabolic correction. Key perpetuating mechanisms, such as sustained AGE-RAGE signaling, persistent mitochondrial DNA damage, and locked histone modifications at pro-inflammatory loci, will be targeted with combination therapies comprising RAGE antagonists, mitochondria-targeted antioxidants, and epigenetic modulators. Therapeutic efficacy will be assessed in the organ-on-a-chip and in vivo models, measuring nerve conduction recovery, axonal regeneration, and resolution of pain phenotypes, thus addressing why current glycemic control strategies fail to fully prevent or reverse established neuropathy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a dual-module '3D genome editor' combining locus-specific WAPL recruitment with epigenetic insulator reinforcement to selectively disrupt pathological enhancer–promoter (E–P) loops. The core innovation is a dCas9-based fusion protein that recruits a WAPL functional domain specifically to disease-associated cohesin-occupied E–P anchor sites, locally accelerating cohesin unloading to dissolve the aberrant loop without globally perturbing cohesin dynamics. Because WAPL-mediated release acts on the existing cohesin turnover cycle rather than destroying architectural proteins, normal CTCF-anchored loops and TAD boundaries remain intact. A second module, delivered in the same vector, deploys a dCas9 ortholog fused to DNMT3A-3L targeting the pathological enhancer to deposit DNA methylation that prevents re-engagement of transcription factors and Mediator, providing durable silencing after transient WAPL-mediated loop dissolution. The two modules are co-delivered as a single mRNA-lipid nanoparticle payload alongside pre-loaded guide RNAs, requiring only one delivery event. This hit-and-run strategy ensures that WAPL recruitment is transient while the epigenetic mark persists, combining structural protein manipulation with epigenetic memory to achieve selective, lasting E–P loop correction without DNA sequence alteration.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a split-intein proximity-sensing loop disruptor in which two dCas9 halves, each fused to one fragment of a split WAPL effector domain, are targeted to the enhancer and promoter anchors of a pathological loop, respectively. Only when both dCas9 modules bind their cognate sites within a loop does the split intein reconstitute a functional WAPL fragment that locally evicts cohesin, dissolving the aberrant E–P contact. Critically, each half alone is catalytically inert, so cohesin at normal loops — where only one anchor is targeted — remains unaffected, providing an intrinsic coincidence-detection selectivity mechanism. The system is delivered via two adeno-associated virus vectors (two delivery events), one encoding each half with its respective guide RNA. Reconstituted WAPL activity is transient and spatially restricted, preventing global disruption of 3D genome topology. A complementary dCas9-p300-core histone acetyltransferase module at a nearby legitimate CTCF boundary can optionally reinforce the correct TAD insulation, ensuring that normal E–P contacts are maintained after pathological loop disruption.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering a Mediator-interceptor molecule — a bifunctional fusion protein consisting of a dCas9 targeting the pathological enhancer fused to a dominant-negative MED1 intrinsically disordered region (IDR) truncation that retains Mediator tail-module binding capacity but lacks the ability to form productive transcriptional condensates. By occupying the enhancer, this construct intercepts endogenous Mediator complex recruitment and prevents the formation of phase-separated condensates required for E–P loop stabilization and transcriptional activation at the pathological locus. The dominant-negative MED1-IDR disrupts only the condensate-dependent loop at the targeted site, while normal E–P contacts — which rely on their own local transcription factor–Mediator interactions at untargeted loci — remain unperturbed. The construct is delivered as modified mRNA in a single lipid nanoparticle dose, providing transient expression sufficient to destabilize the aberrant condensate. As a secondary mechanism, a dCas9-KRAB fusion co-expressed from the same mRNA deposits H3K9me3 at the enhancer for longer-term silencing, preventing loop re-formation after Mediator-interceptor clearance.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a locus-targeted cohesin roadblock strategy using catalytically dead Cas12a (dCas12a) programmed with a CRISPR array to simultaneously bind multiple sites flanking the pathological enhancer, creating a physical barrier that arrests cohesin-mediated loop extrusion before it reaches the pathological E–P contact point. By placing multiple dCas12a molecules as synthetic extrusion barriers upstream of the aberrant enhancer, cohesin is halted and released before it can bring the enhancer into proximity with the oncogenic promoter. Normal loops anchored by endogenous CTCF sites elsewhere in the TAD are unaffected because the synthetic barriers are positioned exclusively within the pathological sub-loop. A complementary module consisting of dCas9-TET1 can demethylate a silenced or weakened CTCF boundary site between the enhancer and promoter, restoring normal insulation. The entire system requires two delivery events: one AAV encoding the dCas12a with its CRISPR array and one mRNA encoding dCas9-TET1 with its guide RNA. This approach achieves structural correction without altering DNA sequence and preserves global 3D genome organization.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a chromatin loop editor based on targeted NIPBL eviction from pathological cohesin loading sites. Recent evidence shows that cohesin loading by the NIPBL-MAU2 complex at enhancer-proximal sites is critical for E–P loop formation. Our tool employs a dCas9 fused to a NIPBL-competitive peptide — derived from the NIPBL interaction surface with the cohesin SMC hinge — that is guided to the pathological enhancer where it blocks NIPBL-mediated cohesin loading specifically at that locus. Without local cohesin loading, the loop extrusion events that bring the pathological enhancer to its aberrant promoter target cannot initiate, while CTCF-anchored structural loops loaded from other sites remain intact. As a secondary mechanism, dCas9-HDAC3 fusion is co-delivered to deacetylate H3K27ac at the pathological enhancer, further reducing its activity and Mediator recruitment. The two components are delivered as a single polycistronic mRNA via lipid nanoparticles, constituting one delivery event. This approach uniquely targets the initiation rather than the maintenance of pathological loops, offering a preventive rather than purely disruptive paradigm for 3D genome correction.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a condensate-dissolving 3D genome editor that targets the phase-separated transcriptional condensates specifically sustaining pathological E–P loops. The tool consists of a dCas9 fused to an engineered anti-condensate peptide — a polyanion-rich low-complexity domain designed to competitively partition into and disassemble MED1/BRD4-driven condensates at disease-specific super-enhancers without affecting normal enhancers that lack super-enhancer-scale condensate architecture. The dCas9 guides the anti-condensate effector exclusively to the pathological super-enhancer, where it dissolves the condensate hub maintaining the aberrant E–P loop while normal E–P contacts governed by standard Mediator bridging or CTCF-cohesin loops remain unaffected. As an epigenetic reinforcement, a second dCas9 ortholog fused to EZH2 deposits H3K27me3 at the pathological enhancer to provide Polycomb-mediated silencing after condensate dissolution. Both modules are delivered as a dual-component mRNA in a single lipid nanoparticle, requiring one delivery event. This approach exploits the biophysical vulnerability unique to pathological condensate-dependent loops, achieving selectivity through the distinct material properties of disease-associated versus normal regulatory hubs.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a synthetic CTCF neo-insulator strategy for correcting pathological E–P loops caused by boundary loss or enhancer hijacking. The tool deploys a catalytically inactive dCas9 fused to a minimal CTCF zinc-finger array (ZF4-7) that retains cohesin-stalling capacity but lacks the RNA-binding and dimerization domains of full-length CTCF, preventing ectopic loop formation. Guided by sgRNAs to the breakpoint or boundary-loss region between a hijacked enhancer and its aberrant promoter target, the dCas9-CTCF(ZF4-7) fusion creates a de novo extrusion barrier that re-insulates the two elements into separate topological neighborhoods. A complementary dCas9-DNMT3A module methylates the pathological enhancer-proximal CTCF-independent anchor to further weaken any residual aberrant E–P contact. The two modules can be delivered as dual AAV vectors (two delivery events), each encoding one dCas9 ortholog with its respective guide RNAs. This approach uniquely restores boundary function rather than simply disrupting loops, representing a corrective rather than ablative paradigm for 3D genome editing that preserves and indeed actively reconstitutes normal chromatin architecture.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an RNA-guided cohesin modifier that exploits the recently discovered role of CTCF zinc-finger 1 (ZF1)-RNA interactions in maintaining cell-type-specific chromatin loops. The tool consists of a programmable antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) that degrades a specific lncRNA or eRNA required for stabilizing CTCF binding at the anchor of a pathological E–P loop, combined with a dCas9-recruited RNA decoy that sequesters any residual transcript. Loss of the stabilizing RNA at the pathological CTCF anchor destabilizes CTCF occupancy, allowing cohesin to read through and dissolve the aberrant loop, while CTCF sites anchoring normal loops — which rely on different RNA partners or RNA-independent mechanisms — remain intact. The ASO and dCas9 decoy are delivered together as a single lipid nanoparticle payload (one delivery event). As an epigenetic backup, the dCas9 module also carries a KRAB domain to deposit H3K9me3 at the destabilized anchor for sustained silencing. This approach leverages the inherent RNA-dependence of specific CTCF loops as a selectivity filter, offering a novel molecular handle for loop-specific disruption without altering DNA sequence or broadly perturbing structural proteins.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a multi-output synthetic gene circuit housed in microencapsulated engineered human cells that senses circulating leptin as a proxy for adiposity and coordinately produces three therapeutic effectors when leptin exceeds a calibrated threshold. The sensor module employs a chimeric transcription factor comprising the extracellular and transmembrane domains of the human leptin receptor fused to an orthogonal split-intein-mediated transcriptional activator, tuned via synthetic signal amplification to distinguish pathological hyperleptinemia from normal leptin levels. Above-threshold leptin triggers simultaneous expression of GDF15 (to suppress appetite via brainstem GFRAL signaling), a secreted FGF21 variant (to enhance adipose thermogenesis and hepatic fatty acid oxidation), and an engineered adiponectin multimer (to promote glucose disposal into skeletal muscle and limit de novo lipogenesis). An integral negative-feedback loop is encoded by a SOCS3-mimetic module that attenuates circuit activity as leptin levels normalize following weight loss, preventing undershoot. The entire circuit is delivered subcutaneously within alginate-poly-L-lysine microcapsules, permitting immune isolation and retrieval. This design addresses the biological asymmetry of energy homeostasis by installing a de novo anti-weight-gain arm that is absent in common obesity yet self-limiting at a healthy set point.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering autologous human white adipocyte progenitors ex vivo with a Piezo1-gated synthetic gene circuit that converts the mechanical signal of adipocyte hypertrophy into a tri-modal anti-obesity response. As adipocytes enlarge beyond a defined lipid-loading threshold, increased membrane tension activates the endogenous mechanosensitive channel Piezo1, driving calcium influx that is intercepted by a synthetic calcineurin-NFAT signaling module rewired to a NFAT-responsive synthetic promoter. This promoter drives a polycistronic cassette encoding a secreted alpha-MSH analog (for centrally mediated appetite suppression), UCP1 (for cell-autonomous thermogenesis and energy expenditure), and a dominant-negative DGAT2 fragment (to block triglyceride synthesis and reroute fatty acids toward oxidation). Because Piezo1 activation scales with cell volume, the circuit output self-adjusts proportionally to fat mass expansion and silences as adipocytes return to normal size. Ex vivo CRISPR editing and autologous reimplantation of progenitors into subcutaneous fat avoids immunogenicity and enables durable engraftment. This mechanosensory design uniquely leverages the physical correlate of fat gain rather than circulating hormones, providing a cell-autonomous, robust, and tamper-resistant fat mass sensor.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a liver-targeted adeno-associated virus delivering a synthetic fatty-acid-gated transcriptional circuit that outputs three coordinated anti-obesity signals when hepatic lipid influx exceeds a healthy threshold. The sensor is a redesigned PPARalpha ligand-binding domain fused to a synthetic DNA-binding domain and a transcriptional activation domain, engineered with a right-shifted dose-response curve so that the circuit activates only at supraphysiological intrahepatic fatty acid concentrations typical of obesity. Upon activation, the circuit drives expression of GLP-1 (to suppress appetite and enhance insulin secretion), irisin (to promote white-adipose-tissue browning and increase energy expenditure), and ANGPTL4 (to inhibit lipoprotein lipase activity in adipose tissue and redirect circulating triglycerides away from fat storage toward oxidative tissues). Hepatic miR-122-responsive destabilization elements in the construct's 3'-UTR further confine expression to hepatocytes. An embedded negative feedback loop, where ANGPTL4-driven fatty acid redistribution lowers intrahepatic lipid levels, ensures self-termination of the circuit as metabolic parameters normalize. This approach exploits the liver's role as a metabolic sensor and secretory organ to generate systemically acting hormones from a single, clinically feasible AAV vector.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a subcutaneously implanted cell-based therapeutic platform in which iPSC-derived beige adipocytes are engineered with a synthetic hypoxia-responsive anti-obesity circuit. Adipose tissue expansion during obesity produces tissue hypoxia due to insufficient angiogenesis, and this pathological feature is exploited as the circuit's input signal. A synthetic promoter containing multimerized hypoxia response elements, tuned to activate only below severe physiological pO2 thresholds characteristic of obese adipose depots, drives a tricistronic cassette encoding a stabilized leptin sensitizer (a secreted SOCS3 decoy peptide that restores hypothalamic leptin signaling to suppress appetite), PRDM16 (to cell-autonomously activate the thermogenic beige adipocyte program and increase energy expenditure), and a secreted form of IL-15 (to promote skeletal muscle fatty acid oxidation and lean mass preservation, thereby repartitioning nutrients). As weight loss alleviates adipose hypoxia, the hypoxia-responsive promoter is silenced and the circuit self-terminates. Encapsulation of these cells in immunoprotective hydrogel devices allows for transplantation without immunosuppression. This strategy uniquely exploits a disease-specific microenvironmental cue rather than a systemic biomarker, offering spatially resolved and proportionally graded circuit activation.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle platform for periodic adipose-targeted delivery of a synthetic proportional-control circuit that restores anti-weight-gain homeostasis. The circuit mRNA encodes a self-contained intracellular sensor-effector system: a chimeric transcription factor consisting of a lipid-droplet-coat-protein (perilipin-1) targeting domain fused to a lipid-droplet-size-sensitive conformational switch and a transcriptional activator. In hypertrophic adipocytes, the enlarged lipid droplet surface exposes the chimeric factor, enabling its nuclear translocation and activation of co-delivered effector mRNAs encoding GDF15 (appetite suppression), a constitutively active AMPK variant (stimulation of fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial biogenesis), and ATGL/adipose triglyceride lipase (enhanced lipolysis redirecting fatty acids from storage to oxidation). Adipose-tropic lipid nanoparticles incorporating three-tailed phosphoramidate lipids and prohibitin-targeting peptides ensure selective delivery to white adipose depots upon subcutaneous injection. Because the circuit components are mRNA-based and transient, dosing frequency can be adjusted to clinical need, providing a tunable and reversible therapeutic window. This non-viral, non-permanent approach addresses key translational barriers of gene therapy while preserving closed-loop proportional control over adiposity.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an AAV-delivered synthetic gene circuit targeting arcuate nucleus neurons that reinstalls a weight-gain defense by coupling an adiposity-proportional sensor to melanocortin pathway activation. The circuit employs a synthetic leptin-responsive promoter containing optimized STAT3 binding elements paired with an engineered SOCS3-insensitive leptin receptor variant (LepR-Y985F/Y1077F), rendering the sensor resistant to the obesity-associated desensitization that normally silences the endogenous system. Above a defined leptin threshold, the circuit drives expression of three effectors from the same cassette: a stabilized alpha-MSH peptide (MC4R agonist for appetite suppression and sympathetic activation), BDNF (to enhance energy expenditure through thermogenesis and locomotor activity), and a secreted dominant-negative AgRP decoy (to prevent endogenous AgRP from antagonizing MC4R). Stereotactic AAV delivery to the arcuate nucleus using neuron-specific synapsin promoter elements confines expression to the appropriate hypothalamic neurons. The circuit's proportional output inherently scales with fat mass via the leptin signal, and resistance to SOCS3-mediated shutdown overcomes the central leptin resistance that prevents endogenous defense against weight gain. This neurocentric approach directly targets the site where the biological asymmetry between weight-loss and weight-gain defense originates.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering a synthetic intercellular adipose-muscle communication circuit using two populations of engineered cells that together recapitulate and strengthen the missing anti-weight-gain arm of energy homeostasis. The first module consists of adipose-resident sentinel cells (microencapsulated HEK293-derived designer cells) harboring a synthetic intracellular lipid-sensing receptor that detects elevated free fatty acid levels and outputs a secreted engineered cytokine, a hyperactive IL-6 variant selectively biased toward AMPK-activating signaling in skeletal muscle. The second module employs muscle-tropic AAV-delivered synthetic receptors in skeletal myocytes that respond to this designer cytokine by activating PGC-1alpha expression (increasing oxidative metabolism and energy expenditure) and secreting irisin (promoting white adipose browning and enhanced thermogenesis), while simultaneously upregulating GLUT4 to divert glucose from lipogenic pathways. A quorum-sensing-inspired feedback element ensures the circuit self-attenuates: irisin-driven browning reduces the fatty acid overflow that activates the sentinel cells. This two-tissue, two-vector architecture mimics the physiological organ crosstalk that obesity disrupts, modulating all three required axes—appetite (via IL-6 hypothalamic action), energy expenditure (via PGC-1alpha and browning), and nutrient partitioning (via GLUT4 and fat oxidation)—while distributing the circuit load to avoid overloading any single tissue.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a synthetic epigenetic-reset circuit that selectively de-represses the silenced anti-obesity gene programs in adipose tissue when body fat exceeds a healthy set point. The circuit is delivered via adipose-tropic AAV encoding a fusion protein comprising the catalytic domain of TET2 (a DNA demethylase) fused to a programmable CRISPR-dCas9 scaffold guided by a panel of sgRNAs targeting the methylated promoters of UCP1, PRDM16, and adiponectin in white adipocytes. Expression of the TET2-dCas9 construct is placed under the control of a synthetic promoter activated by NF-kappaB, which is chronically elevated in hypertrophic, inflamed adipose tissue of obese individuals but quiescent in lean adipose depots. Upon activation, targeted demethylation reactivates UCP1 and PRDM16 to drive thermogenic reprogramming (increasing energy expenditure), restores adiponectin secretion (improving insulin sensitivity and redirecting nutrients toward oxidative disposal), and the resulting adipose tissue remodeling reduces NF-kappaB-driven inflammation, thereby self-silencing the circuit. This approach simultaneously addresses all three output axes by correcting the obesity-associated epigenetic lock rather than imposing exogenous effectors, offering a durable yet self-limiting therapeutic intervention with a clear path to clinical translation via established AAV and CRISPR technologies.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering hPSC-CM tissues that combine the MEDUSA quadruple gene edit (HCN4/CACNA1H/SLC8A1 knockout plus KCNJ2 overexpression) with a second-layer calcium-clock silencing module consisting of CRISPR-mediated heterozygous knockdown of RyR2 diastolic leak and constitutive overexpression of SERCA2a. The MEDUSA edit eliminates the membrane voltage clock but leaves the calcium clock partially intact, which may re-emerge under catecholaminergic stimulation or ischemic calcium overload. By suppressing spontaneous sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release without eliminating stimulus-dependent calcium-induced calcium release, this dual-layer design should maintain contractile force upon host-driven excitation while eliminating residual automaticity under adrenergic stress. Engineered heart tissues would be fabricated from these cells in aligned collagen hydrogels and subjected to systematic provocation protocols including isoproterenol challenge, simulated ischemia-reperfusion, and hyperkalemia. Tissue-level quiescence and stimulus-response fidelity would be verified by high-density optical mapping and compared against MEDUSA-only controls in a porcine chronic infarct model with telemetric monitoring over twelve weeks.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a synthetic-biology approach in which a genetic toggle switch hardwires KCNJ2 and KCNJ12 expression to a constitutively ON state in hPSC-CMs while simultaneously repressing HCN4 through a mutually exclusive bistable circuit based on orthogonal recombinases. Unlike static overexpression, this self-reinforcing genetic architecture ensures that IK1 density is maintained even when transgene silencing pressure, chromatin remodeling during in vivo maturation, or inflammatory signaling would otherwise erode the quiescent phenotype. A CRISPR-integrated positive-feedback loop linking a cardiac-specific promoter to the recombinase sustains the ON state irreversibly upon cardiomyocyte differentiation. We would characterize the bistability margins computationally and experimentally, then fabricate three-dimensional engineered heart tissues and validate tissue-level quiescence over prolonged culture followed by transplantation into infarcted porcine hearts. The robustness of the quiescent state would be tested against isoproterenol infusion, rapid pacing, and acute ischemia, with continuous telemetric electrocardiographic and optical-mapping endpoints quantifying arrhythmia burden relative to non-circuit-bearing controls.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose designing quiescent engineered myocardial tissues using hPSC-CMs in which pacemaker-associated proteins HCN4 and CACNA1H are tagged with an auxin-inducible degron, providing rapid, tunable, and reversible post-translational silencing of automaticity that does not depend on transcriptional knockdown or permanent gene deletion. Auxin (indole-3-acetic acid) is a small bioorthogonal molecule already validated in mammalian cells that would be administered systemically or released locally from a hydrogel scaffold co-transplanted with the tissue. This strategy preserves the genomic locus intact, allowing the cell to potentially mature toward an adult ventricular phenotype over time. We would combine degron-tagged HCN4 and CACNA1H with stable KCNJ2 knock-in to set a hyperpolarized resting potential as a constitutive safety floor. Tissue constructs would be tested for their ability to remain quiescent during auxin dosing, follow external pacing without conduction delay, and contract with force comparable to unmodified controls, both in vitro under catecholamine and acidosis challenge and in vivo in a porcine infarct model over eight weeks.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a tissue-architecture-first strategy that exploits the electrotonic sink effect of Cx43-overexpressing cardiac fibroblasts to suppress automaticity at the tissue level without any ion-channel modification of the cardiomyocytes. Engineered heart tissues would be fabricated by co-seeding hPSC-CMs with iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts engineered to constitutively overexpress Cx43 at defined ratios and in spatially controlled patterns within an aligned fibrin hydrogel. The non-excitable fibroblasts, coupled to cardiomyocytes via abundant gap junctions, act as a distributed electrotonic load that clamps the diastolic depolarization of adjacent immature cardiomyocytes below the threshold for spontaneous firing, while still permitting propagation of a host-driven wavefront. We would systematically vary the fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte ratio and spatial distribution using micropatterning, map tissue-level automaticity and conduction velocity by optical voltage imaging, and identify an optimal configuration that suppresses spontaneous activity without reducing conduction velocity below a critical threshold. This optimized design would then be transplanted intramyocardially into a porcine infarct model and monitored for arrhythmia burden, host-graft synchrony, and contractile contribution.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose fabricating anisotropic, pre-coupled engineered heart tissue strips from KCNJ2-overexpressing hPSC-CMs on electrospun aligned conductive polycaprolactone-carbon nanotube scaffolds designed for intramural implantation rather than epicardial placement, thereby maximizing the graft-host contact interface and accelerating gap-junction-mediated electrical integration. Prior work shows that epicardial patches frequently remain electrically uncoupled from host myocardium due to intervening scar, whereas intramyocardially delivered constructs achieve rapid coupling. Our innovation combines the pro-quiescent electrophysiology of KCNJ2-overexpressing cells with a scaffold architecture that maintains tissue-scale alignment and mechanical integrity during needle-based intramural delivery. The conductive scaffold itself provides a low-resistance pathway within the graft, ensuring uniform activation upon host-driven wavefront arrival even before biological gap junctions fully mature. We would characterize conduction velocity, anisotropy ratio, and automaticity of these constructs in vitro under pacing, catecholamine, and ischemia-mimicking protocols, then test them in a porcine chronic infarct model using GCaMP-based calcium imaging and electroanatomical mapping to quantify coupling latency, synchrony, and arrhythmia incidence over twelve weeks.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a combinatorial maturation-plus-suppression protocol in which hPSC-CMs are subjected to an accelerated electromechanical maturation regimen (ramped electrical pacing, triiodothyronine treatment, fatty acid supplementation, and micropatterned alignment) while simultaneously receiving lentiviral delivery of KCNJ2 and shRNA against HCN4, before being assembled into three-dimensional engineered heart tissues. Prior work has shown that combinatorial maturation cues can increase the fraction of quiescent-yet-excitable preparations to over seventy percent; we hypothesize that pairing this approach with targeted suppression of residual pacemaker currents can achieve near-complete tissue-level quiescence that is robust to subsequent adrenergic stimulation. The matured tissue would possess adult-like sodium-channel density and IK1, ensuring high conduction velocity and excitability, while the developmental down-regulation of HCN channels is genetically locked in. We would benchmark these tissues against MEDUSA and maturation-only controls using multi-electrode array and optical mapping under baseline, isoproterenol, hyperkalemia, and simulated-ischemia conditions, then transplant into infarcted porcine hearts with chronic telemetric monitoring and stress testing to evaluate arrhythmia burden and contractile function.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering a graft-autonomous anti-arrhythmia safeguard by incorporating a calcium-sensing synthetic gene circuit into hPSC-CMs that activates expression of an inhibitory potassium channel (engineered Kir2.1 variant with fast membrane trafficking) in response to sustained elevations in intracellular calcium, a hallmark of ectopic automaticity and triggered activity. This circuit would use a calcineurin-NFAT-responsive synthetic promoter linked to expression of a membrane-targeted Kir2.1 fused to a short-half-life degron, ensuring that the protective current activates only during pathological calcium accumulation and is rapidly cleared when calcium normalizes. The feedback architecture provides a tissue-level guarantee: any cell or cluster entering a pro-automatic state would self-correct by increasing its own repolarization reserve. We would build and characterize this circuit in hPSC-CMs, demonstrating that it does not impair baseline excitation-contraction coupling, then incorporate circuit-bearing cells into engineered heart tissues and challenge them with isoproterenol, rapid pacing, and simulated ischemia-reperfusion. In vivo validation would employ porcine intramyocardial transplantation with telemetric arrhythmia monitoring.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering hPSC-CM-based myocardial tissues with a Cx43-enriched graft-host interface zone created by bioprinting a gradient border region of cardiomyocytes co-transduced with Cx43 and Nav1.5 (SCN5A) overexpression cassettes, transitioning into a core region of KCNJ2-overexpressing quiescent cardiomyocytes. This biomimetic architecture addresses the critical vulnerability window immediately post-transplantation when sparse gap junctions between graft and host create regions of source-sink mismatch and conduction block that can trigger re-entry. The border-zone cells would provide enhanced coupling conductance and sodium current to ensure rapid source current delivery into the graft interior, while the quiescent core cells provide contractile mass without autonomous rhythm generation. We would optimize the gradient width and expression levels computationally using a bidomain electrophysiology model, then fabricate the heterogeneous tissues by multi-material bioprinting in aligned fibrin-collagen hydrogels, and validate them in vitro by optical mapping and in vivo by intramyocardial implantation in porcine infarcts with serial electroanatomical mapping and cardiac MRI over twelve weeks.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a dual-compartment injectable hydrogel system that simultaneously reinforces dermal ECM and subcutaneous fibrous septa during pharmacological weight loss without impeding lipolysis. The platform consists of a thermo-responsive, in situ cross-linking hyaluronic acid–poly-L-lactic acid composite hydrogel loaded with two bioactive payloads: (i) collagen-binding synthetic peptidoglycans that shield existing collagen and elastin fibrils from MMP-mediated degradation by physically masking cleavage sites, and (ii) recombinant LOXL1 enzyme that catalyzes de novo cross-linking of nascent tropoelastin and procollagen, strengthening both the dermal matrix and the collagenous septa of subcutaneous fat compartments. Delivered in one to three sessions via structured subcutaneous and intradermal injection grids, the hydrogel degrades over 8–12 weeks, providing sustained local release while PLLA microparticles stimulate endogenous neocollagenesis via macrophage-mediated fibroblast activation. Because the peptidoglycan–LOXL1 strategy targets structural ECM proteins rather than adipocyte metabolism, lipolysis proceeds unhindered. Preliminary feasibility can be assessed in diet-induced obese murine models with serial elastometry, collagen quantification, and fat mass tracking.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a microneedle patch–delivered lipid nanoparticle system encoding multiplexed mRNAs for TIMP-1, tropoelastin, and decorin, designed to be applied in few sessions during active weight loss to simultaneously protect dermal collagen from proteolytic degradation and reinforce subcutaneous septal architecture. Ionizable LNPs are formulated with fibroblast-targeting peptide ligands to ensure preferential uptake by dermal and septal fibroblasts after intradermal microneedle delivery, bypassing epidermal immune cells. TIMP-1 mRNA suppresses weight-loss-induced MMP-1 and MMP-13 upregulation to shield existing collagen networks; tropoelastin mRNA directly replenishes elastic fiber precursors; and decorin mRNA promotes proper collagen fibrillogenesis while sequestering TGF-beta to prevent pathological fibrosis of deflating fat compartments. Trans-amplifying RNA technology extends intracellular expression to approximately seven days per application, reducing treatment frequency. This gene-therapy-light approach leverages clinically validated LNP chemistry and dissolving microneedle fabrication, offering a realistic regulatory path as a combination biologic device with strong patentability based on the novel multi-cargo and targeting strategy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose targeted senolytic clearance of senescent fibroblasts and adipocytes in skin and subcutaneous tissue during GLP-1-agonist-induced weight loss, combined with autologous adipose-derived stem cell exosome infusion, to reset the dermal and hypodermal microenvironment for adaptive ECM remodeling rather than structural collapse. Senescent cells accumulating in stretched or inflamed skin and shrinking adipose depots secrete SASP factors (IL-6, TNF-alpha, MMPs) that degrade collagen, elastin, and fibrous septa. A short course (three sessions over twelve weeks) of locally injected dasatinib-quercetin nanoparticles in a slow-release PLGA matrix selectively eliminates senescent cells while sparing functional adipocytes and fibroblasts. Concurrently, exosomes harvested from the patient's own lipoaspirate-derived stem cells are co-delivered intradermally, supplying miR-29a, TGF-beta3, and antioxidant cargo that stimulate fibroblast proliferation, enhance collagen-III and elastin synthesis, and suppress inflammatory remodeling. This dual clearance-and-replenishment strategy uniquely addresses the root cellular pathology driving both dermal laxity and septal weakening, while lipolysis pathways remain intact. The approach is clinically translatable using existing senolytic compounds and point-of-care exosome processing systems.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose the development of a collagen-anchored, bifunctional fusion protein comprising an engineered TIMP-3 domain fused to a decorin core protein fragment, delivered as a single subcutaneous depot injection in a thermosensitive chitosan-beta-glycerophosphate hydrogel to simultaneously inhibit matrix metalloproteinase activity and reinforce collagen fibril architecture in both dermal and subcutaneous compartments during weight loss. The TIMP-3 domain provides broad-spectrum, ECM-bound MMP inhibition that is self-localizing to collagen-rich tissues (dermis and fibrous septa) via the decorin collagen-binding leucine-rich repeat, ensuring selectivity without systemic exposure. The decorin moiety additionally sequesters TGF-beta to prevent fibrotic contraction of deflating fat compartment walls and promotes orderly collagen fibrillogenesis. The thermosensitive hydrogel gels at body temperature after injection, forming a sustained-release reservoir lasting six to eight weeks from a single administration. This design addresses both the proteolytic and architectural arms of skin structural deterioration and offers clear advantages in patentability as a novel fusion protein with dual mechanism. Preclinical validation in a murine diet-induced obesity weight-loss model would assess dermal thickness, elasticity, septal collagen density, and total fat mass concurrently.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a programmable focused-ultrasound platform that delivers spatially patterned mechanical stimulation to the dermis and subcutaneous septae, activating endogenous fibroblast mechanotransduction via the YAP/TAZ pathway to induce adaptive ECM synthesis during weight loss without tissue ablation. Unlike existing radiofrequency or high-intensity focused ultrasound devices that rely on thermal tissue injury and wound healing, this system uses sub-ablative, pulsed acoustic radiation force at two calibrated focal depths—dermal (1–2 mm) and hypodermal septal planes (5–10 mm)—to selectively activate integrin-FAK-YAP signaling in fibroblasts, upregulating collagen I, collagen III, and elastin transcription while avoiding adipocyte damage or inflammatory MMP cascades. Acoustic parameters are guided by real-time B-mode and elastography imaging to map tissue planes. Three to five treatment sessions spaced over the weight-loss period would be sufficient, as YAP-driven matrix synthesis persists weeks after mechanical stimulus. This device-based approach carries favorable regulatory precedent, requires no exogenous biologics, and its novelty lies in the dual-depth, sub-ablative mechanotransduction paradigm specifically designed for the weight-loss context.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an injectable, slow-degrading electrospun polycaprolactone nano-fibrous scaffold mimicking the architecture of subcutaneous fibrous septa, co-loaded with GHK-Cu tripeptide and vitamin C palmitate, designed to be implanted into the subcutaneous layer via large-bore needle injection in one to two sessions to provide both mechanical support and biochemical stimulation during fat volume reduction. The aligned nanofiber architecture serves as a temporary structural replacement for thinning septa, maintaining compartmentalization and dermal-to-fascial tethering as adipocyte volume decreases. GHK-Cu stimulates endogenous fibroblast migration, collagen deposition, and lysyl oxidase expression for new cross-linked collagen and elastin assembly on the scaffold template, while ascorbyl palmitate serves as a cofactor for prolyl hydroxylase, enhancing collagen stability. The scaffold degrades over six to nine months, by which time endogenous fibrous tissue has replaced it. This approach is distinct from dermal fillers in that it provides architectural guidance rather than volume, and its novelty lies in the biomimetic septal scaffold concept with integrated matrikine release. Feasibility studies would employ a porcine panniculus model with serial imaging and histomorphometry.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a topically applied, penetration-enhanced cream formulation delivering a selective MMP-2/MMP-9 inhibitor combined with recombinant human tropoelastin microparticles, designed for daily use during pharmacological weight loss to protect and rebuild dermal elastic fiber networks and basement membrane collagen IV integrity. MMP-2 and MMP-9 are the principal gelatinases upregulated during mechanical unloading of previously stretched skin, degrading type IV collagen at the dermal-epidermal junction and elastin in the papillary dermis, thereby contributing to both skin fragility and loss of recoil. A hydroxamate-based, next-generation selective gelatinase inhibitor formulated in a deformable liposomal carrier achieves dermal penetration without systemic absorption. Co-delivered tropoelastin microparticles, deposited in microneedle-created channels during weekly at-home microneedling, serve as substrates for endogenous LOX-mediated cross-linking into mature elastic fibers. This combination addresses the elastic component of skin laxity that collagen-centric approaches miss. The formulation would be evaluated in a clinical pilot study of patients undergoing GLP-1 agonist therapy, with serial skin elasticity measurements, ultrasound dermal thickness mapping, and MMP zymography from tape-stripped samples.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an epigenetic reprogramming strategy using intradermal delivery of a cocktail of microRNAs (miR-29a mimic, miR-196a inhibitor, and miR-21 inhibitor) encapsulated in dermis-tropic extracellular vesicles, to coordinately shift the dermal fibroblast secretome from a catabolic, MMP-dominant state to an anabolic, ECM-synthetic state during the inflammatory milieu that accompanies rapid fat loss. MiR-29a directly represses collagen-degrading pathways including TGF-beta-activated kinase 1 binding protein and multiple collagen transcriptional suppressors, while miR-196a inhibition derepresses COL1A1 and COL3A1 transcription, and miR-21 inhibition reduces SMAD7-mediated blockade of pro-fibrogenic TGF-beta signaling in the dermis without promoting pathological fibrosis when balanced by miR-29a. Delivered via dissolvable hyaluronic acid microneedle patches at monthly intervals during weight loss, the microRNA cargo is protected within engineered extracellular vesicles displaying fibroblast-binding integrins. This systems-level transcriptomic intervention addresses the root gene-regulatory imbalance rather than single molecular targets, offering durable matrix protection. Its novelty resides in the rationally designed multi-miRNA cocktail specifically optimized for the weight-loss-associated catabolic skin phenotype.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a unified post-HSCT monitoring assay termed MitoChimer-seq, which combines targeted deep sequencing of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) heteroplasmic variants with a curated panel of donor-recipient informative nuclear SNPs, performed on FACS-sorted hematopoietic lineage fractions (CD3+ T cells, CD19+ B cells, CD14+ monocytes, CD66b+ granulocytes, glycophorin-A+ erythroblasts, and CD41+ megakaryocytic progenitors) from peripheral blood. The nuclear SNP panel provides quantitative chimerism at lineage-specific resolution, while the mtDNA heteroplasmic variant profile—leveraging the high mutation rate and natural clonal barcode properties of the mitochondrial genome—independently measures polyclonal diversity by enumerating distinct donor-derived clonal lineages contributing to each compartment. We will develop a composite Engraftment-Diversity Index computed from both readouts, enabling detection of oligoclonal reconstitution patterns that precede graft failure or relapse. The amplicon-based design allows multiplexed processing on standard Illumina platforms with a 48-hour turnaround and is compatible with minimal blood volumes, supporting monthly longitudinal sampling over one year. We will validate this approach in a prospective cohort of 60 allogeneic HSCT recipients, benchmarking against STR chimerism and TCR repertoire sequencing.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose EpiEngraft, a clinically translatable assay that exploits stochastic somatic CpG methylation variation (epimutations) at carefully selected intermediately methylated regions as endogenous clonal barcodes to simultaneously quantify donor chimerism and clonal diversity after HSCT. Building on the principle that epimutations at specific CpG loci are heritable through cell division yet arise independently in different stem cell clones, we will design a targeted bisulfite-sequencing panel of approximately 500 informative CpGs optimized for clonal discrimination and lineage-state readout. The assay is applied to immunomagnetically sorted hematopoietic lineage fractions—myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic—from peripheral blood or bone marrow. A Bayesian clustering algorithm deconvolves methylation haplotypes into clone identities and estimates both donor fraction and Shannon diversity indices at each time point. Longitudinal profiling at monthly intervals over 12 months enables tracking of clonal dynamics including early detection of oligoclonality. The targeted panel approach on bisulfite-converted DNA uses standard sequencing infrastructure, achieving practical cost and turnaround benchmarks suitable for clinical adoption.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose HaploClone-seq, a novel multiplex amplicon sequencing method that targets approximately 200 microhaplotype loci—short genomic windows containing two to four phased SNPs—selected for high heterozygosity across diverse populations and distributed across all autosomes. Unlike standard biallelic SNP or STR chimerism assays, microhaplotypes provide multiallelic discrimination power, enabling simultaneous determination of donor-versus-recipient origin and enumeration of distinct contributing haplotype clones within the donor graft. The assay is performed on six immunomagnetically sorted lineage fractions from peripheral blood, covering myeloid, T-cell, B-cell, NK-cell, erythroid precursor, and megakaryocytic compartments. Deep sequencing at greater than 10,000x coverage per amplicon enables sensitive detection of minor clonal populations contributing as little as 0.1 percent of a lineage. A dedicated bioinformatic pipeline reconstructs haplotype frequency distributions and computes clonal diversity metrics including effective clone number and evenness. This framework is designed for standard Illumina sequencers with same-week turnaround, enabling longitudinal monthly monitoring across all hematopoietic compartments for up to one year post-transplant.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose NanoChimer-Diversity, a long-read nanopore sequencing-based assay that leverages adaptive sampling to selectively sequence approximately 300 genomic regions enriched for donor-recipient discriminating variants, structural polymorphisms, and methylation signatures simultaneously from sorted hematopoietic lineage populations. The real-time selective sequencing capability of Oxford Nanopore enables enrichment without prior amplification, avoiding PCR bias and preserving native CpG methylation information that serves as an orthogonal clonal identity marker. Within a single sequencing run, the method quantifies donor chimerism via allele-specific variant calls while simultaneously capturing methylation-based clonal fingerprints at linked CpG sites across long reads. Clonal diversity is estimated by joint analysis of phased SNP haplotypes and methylation patterns across contiguous kilobase-scale reads, providing far greater discriminating power than short-read approaches. Application to six sorted lineage fractions—granulocytes, monocytes, T cells, B cells, erythroid precursors, and platelet progenitors—delivers comprehensive multi-lineage assessment. The portable and rapid nature of nanopore sequencing, combined with a 24-hour library-to-result workflow, supports longitudinal monitoring at monthly intervals for clinical translation.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose CRISPR-ChimeriScope, a multiplexed CRISPR-Cas13a fluorescence-based assay that interrogates 96 donor-recipient informative SNP loci and 48 lineage-identity RNA markers in a single reaction from sorted hematopoietic cell populations. Pre-selected crRNA pools targeting high-heterozygosity SNPs are combined with lineage-specific transcript probes in a microwell array format, where Cas13a collateral cleavage of fluorescent reporters generates quantitative signals for each allele. The donor chimerism fraction is calculated from the ratio of donor-specific to recipient-specific allelic signals across informative loci, while multiplexed lineage markers confirm the identity and purity of each sorted fraction spanning myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments. Clonal diversity assessment is achieved by statistical modeling of allele frequency distributions across the informative SNP panel: polyclonal reconstitution produces uniform donor allele frequencies, whereas oligoclonal grafts produce characteristic frequency skewing detectable by information-theoretic metrics. The isothermal, amplification-minimal format enables results within four hours from blood draw, and the assay is deployable on standard microplate fluorescence readers, making it suitable for routine clinical longitudinal monitoring over one year.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose cfDNA-ClonalChimer, a cell-free DNA-based assay that exploits the differential release of cfDNA fragments from all hematopoietic lineages, including short-lived myeloid cells, erythroblasts, and megakaryocytes, into peripheral blood plasma. The method combines ultra-deep targeted sequencing of approximately 150 donor-recipient informative insertion-deletion polymorphisms with computational deconvolution of tissue-of-origin using lineage-specific nucleosome positioning and CpG methylation signatures present on the same cfDNA molecules.
