text: We propose a VCP/p97 co-factor engineering strategy to redirect and enhance the nuclear disaggregase and extraction activity of VCP specifically toward pathological protein aggregates. We will design chimeric VCP adaptor proteins in which the substrate-recognition UBX or UBD domain is replaced by a conformation-selective single-domain antibody (nanobody) that binds aggregated but not monomeric forms of disease proteins such as TDP-43 or tau. This engineered adaptor would recruit endogenous VCP hexamers to nuclear aggregates, stimulating their ATP-dependent unfolding and extraction for proteasomal degradation, a pathway that is naturally operative in the nucleus. Nuclear localization would be ensured by an appended NLS, and aggregate selectivity would be intrinsic to the nanobody's conformational specificity. We will express the chimeric adaptor via AAV in iPSC-derived motor neurons carrying ALS-linked TDP-43 mutations and in tauopathy mouse models, assessing aggregate clearance, monomer preservation, and functional rescue. This approach provides a pharmacologically tunable, autophagy-independent nuclear aggregate clearance mechanism.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a therapeutic RNA oligonucleotide strategy that couples aggregate-selective disaggregation with proteasomal clearance in the nucleus. Building on the discovery that short RNAs can reverse aberrant phase transitions of TDP-43 and FUS, we will design chemically stabilized RNA aptamers that selectively bind the low-complexity domains of aggregated RNA-binding proteins in their misfolded conformation. These aptamers will be conjugated to a synthetic SUMO2-mimetic peptide to induce polySUMOylation of the bound aggregate, channeling it into the RNF4-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome pathway native to the nucleus. Because the aptamers preferentially recognize aggregate-exposed epitopes that are buried in the native monomer, selectivity for pathological species is intrinsic. Delivery will exploit intrathecal administration of chemically modified oligonucleotides, a clinically validated CNS delivery route. We will evaluate aggregate clearance, restoration of nuclear TDP-43 and FUS function, and motor neuron survival in ALS/FTD patient-derived iPSC neurons and in transgenic mouse models.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a strategy to clear nuclear protein aggregates by engineering an aggregate-selective nuclear export pathway that reroutes pathological assemblies to the cytoplasmic autophagy-lysosome system. We will design a bispecific adaptor consisting of an aggregate-binding nanobody fused to a tandem nuclear export signal (NES) recognized by the exportin CRM1/XPO1. This adaptor would coat nuclear oligomers and small aggregates, facilitating their CRM1-dependent transport through nuclear pores into the cytoplasm, where they become substrates for p62/SQSTM1-mediated selective autophagy. Aggregate selectivity is conferred by the nanobody's preferential recognition of misfolded conformers. We will incorporate a degron tag to ensure rapid proteasomal degradation of the adaptor itself when not aggregate-bound, preventing off-target export of native proteins. The system will be validated in iPSC-derived neurons modeling nuclear TDP-43 and polyQ aggregate pathologies, measuring nuclear aggregate clearance, cytoplasmic processing, and neuronal health. This approach uniquely links the nuclear compartment to cytoplasmic degradation systems.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a resorbable, injectable granular hydrogel system comprising functionally distinct microgel sub-populations that together establish a transient tertiary regenerative niche for volumetric muscle loss. Three microgel species are co-injected: (i) pro-inflammatory microgels displaying damage-associated molecular patterns and releasing SDF-1α/CCL2 to recruit monocytes and satellite cells; (ii) pro-myogenic microgels presenting aligned electrospun nanofiber topography and sequentially releasing IL-4, IGF-1, and Wnt7a via hydrolysis-gated compartments to drive M2 macrophage polarization and myoblast differentiation along oriented templates; and (iii) MMP-sensitive sentinel microgels whose crosslinks contain peptide substrates for tissue-remodeling MMPs (MMP-2, MMP-9), such that rising MMP activity during functional matrix maturation triggers their degradation and releases the anti-fibrotic factor decorin while simultaneously removing the scaffold. The sentinel microgels thus create a closed-loop termination signal: as newly deposited and remodeling ECM increases local MMP concentration, the scaffold self-dissolves proportionally to remodeling progress. Spatial organization is achieved through differential microgel stiffness and shape, directing myofiber alignment along the injection axis. This modular, fully resorbable system couples immune staging, progenitor patterning, and autonomous self-termination to functional tissue maturation.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We describe a cell-free, resorbable strategy for critical-size bone defect repair that recapitulates endochondral ossification through a staged mRNA-hydrogel system with a built-in functional termination circuit. An oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel is injected into the defect, encapsulating two populations of lipid nanoparticles: fast-release LNPs carrying mRNA encoding SDF-1 and IL-8 for early MSC and neutrophil recruitment, and slow-release LNPs within PLGA microspheres carrying mRNA for BMP-2 and SOX9 to drive recruited MSCs through chondrogenic then osteogenic differentiation. The hydrogel is crosslinked with bisphosphonate-terminated PEG arms that chelate calcium; as osteoid mineralizes and hydroxyapatite crystallizes, competing calcium sequestration destabilizes the crosslinks, causing the hydrogel to dissolve in proportion to local mineralization. This mineralization-coupled dissolution constitutes a closed-loop self-termination mechanism intrinsically tied to bone formation rather than a pre-set degradation timer. The hydrogel's viscoelasticity and HA-based composition provide initial architectural cues that template periosteal-like organization of recruited progenitors. The approach is entirely cell-free, requires no permanent hardware, and leverages established mRNA-LNP and hydrogel technologies for near-term feasibility.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a resorbable synthetic periosteum system for critical-size bone defects that programs a complete temporal regenerative sequence and terminates autonomously upon functional bone bridging. A bilayer electrospun membrane of fast-degrading poly(glycolide-co-trimethylene carbonate) wraps the defect exterior, providing a boundary condition that spatially confines the regenerative niche while presenting aligned topographical cues for cell organization. The inner fibrous layer incorporates three coaxially electrospun fiber populations with distinct core-shell degradation kinetics releasing, in sequence, (1) HMGB1 and CXCL12 to initiate inflammation and recruit periosteal progenitors, (2) TGF-β3 and FGF-2 to expand progenitors and promote angiogenesis, and (3) BMP-2 and Wnt3a to drive osteogenic differentiation. The membrane backbone is crosslinked via alkaline-phosphatase-cleavable phosphoester bonds: as recruited osteoblasts mature and secrete ALP, they enzymatically dissolve the membrane. This closed-loop mechanism links scaffold termination directly to osteoblast functional maturation rather than passive hydrolysis. The spatial confinement by the outer layer imposes cortical-like geometry on new bone, while the sequential release layers execute a temporally staged repair program from inflammation through remodeling.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We introduce an injectable, fully resorbable supramolecular hydrogel system that creates a self-terminating regenerative niche for volumetric muscle loss by coupling mechanotransduction-based feedback to scaffold dissolution. The hydrogel comprises host-guest crosslinked cyclodextrin-adamantane networks with embedded aligned magnetic nanoparticle chains that impose directional anisotropy upon brief external field application during injection, templating myofiber alignment. Early-phase release of TNF-α and IFN-γ from acid-labile microspheres in the initially low-pH wound environment drives M1 macrophage activation and debris clearance. As pH normalizes, pH-responsive microspheres release IL-10 and IGF-1 to shift macrophage polarization toward M2 and promote satellite cell activation and differentiation. The critical novel element is a strain-responsive self-dissolution mechanism: the supramolecular crosslinks are calibrated so that cyclic mechanical loading characteristic of functional contractile activity in regenerating muscle (frequencies of 1-10 Hz, strains above 5%) progressively dissociates host-guest bonds, causing material dissolution only when the tissue generates physiologically relevant contractile force. This creates an intrinsic closed-loop feedback where scaffold removal is gated by functional muscle restoration rather than a temporal timer.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a programmable DNA-hydrogel niche for critical-size bone defect repair that uses aptamer logic gates to autonomously sense regeneration milestones and execute staged morphogen release. A gelatin-methacrylate hydrogel is photocrosslinked in situ within the defect, embedding DNA-nanostructure payloads: aptamer-locked nanocages that open in response to specific molecular signatures of repair stages. Stage-1 nanocages open in the presence of high TNF-α concentrations (inflammation), releasing PDGF-BB and CXCL12 to recruit MSCs and vascular progenitors. Stage-2 nanocages are locked by aptamers recognizing osteocalcin; as early osteogenic differentiation begins, rising osteocalcin opens these cages to release BMP-7 and VEGF, promoting mineralization and angiogenesis. Stage-3 nanocages respond to sclerostin, a marker of osteocyte maturation, releasing anti-osteoclastogenic OPG to protect new bone and a DNase activator that degrades all remaining DNA structures, triggering hydrogel collapse via DNase-cleavable crosslinkers. This three-gate molecular logic creates an autonomous regenerative program where the biological milieu itself dictates transitions between phases and ultimate scaffold termination, establishing spatial patterning through aptamer-mediated differential growth factor gradients within the hydrogel.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We describe a cell-free strategy that combines synthetic extracellular vesicle mimetics with a resorbable granular scaffold to establish a transient regenerative niche for volumetric muscle loss. Liposomal vesicle mimetics are engineered to display surface CXCR4-binding peptides and carry defined microRNA cargoes: miR-206 and miR-133a to promote myogenesis, and miR-126 and miR-210 to drive angiogenesis. These mimetics are loaded onto microporous annealed particle hydrogel scaffolds composed of elongated PEG-based microgels whose anisotropic shape imposes directional alignment on infiltrating cells, generating architectural patterning without a permanent implant. Temporal staging is achieved by encapsulating anti-inflammatory microRNA mimetics (miR-146a) in fast-degrading microgels and pro-myogenic mimetics in slower-degrading microgels, orchestrating macrophage resolution before myogenic commitment. The scaffold incorporates creatine-kinase-cleavable crosslinks as a self-termination mechanism: creatine kinase, secreted by functional differentiated myofibers, enzymatically cleaves the inter-particle bonds, dissolving the scaffold only once contractile muscle tissue has matured. This approach avoids recombinant protein instability concerns, provides spatial alignment through particle geometry, and couples scaffold dissolution to a direct functional biomarker of muscle regeneration.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a resorbable piezoelectric-hydrogel composite that establishes a transient regenerative niche in critical-size bone defects through endogenous bioelectric signaling and load-sensing self-termination. A collagen-alginate hydrogel loaded with poly-L-lactic acid piezoelectric nanofibers is injected into the defect and crosslinked in situ via calcium-mediated gelation. Physiological micro-movements generate local piezoelectric potentials that recruit MSCs via electrotaxis, promote osteogenic differentiation through calcium-channel activation, and drive macrophage M2 polarization. The hydrogel contains compartmentalized PLGA microspheres releasing SDF-1α early and BMP-2 late, providing a biochemical temporal program overlaid on the bioelectric cues. The aligned piezoelectric nanofibers additionally template directional cell organization mimicking Haversian canal geometry. The self-termination mechanism is intrinsically mechanical: as mineralized bone matrix forms and stiffens, it shields the piezoelectric fibers from deformation, silencing the bioelectric signal and simultaneously enabling hydrolytic degradation of the now-unloaded PLLA fibers. Thus the scaffold functionally self-terminates when the regenerated bone assumes the mechanical load, creating a closed-loop linkage between structural restoration and niche dissolution that requires no external sensing or pre-set timer.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We describe an injectable two-component reactive system that self-assembles a transient regenerative niche in volumetric muscle loss defects via in situ bioorthogonal coacervation. Component A is an aqueous solution of tetrazine-functionalized gelatin bearing pendant SDF-1α and Notch-ligand peptides; Component B is a suspension of trans-cyclooctene-functionalized hyaluronic acid microdroplets loaded with IGF-1, HGF, and IL-4 within core-shell PLGA microparticles of varying degradation rates. Upon co-injection and mixing in the defect, inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder click chemistry covalently anneals the components within minutes, forming a porous, architecturally patterned hydrogel whose local stiffness gradients direct satellite cell alignment along the muscle axis. The Notch-ligand presentation maintains recruited satellite cells in a progenitor-expansion state before the delayed release of differentiation factors from slow-degrading microparticles. The network incorporates MMP-14-cleavable crosslinks as a self-termination sensor: MMP-14 is specifically upregulated by myotubes during basement membrane remodeling, linking scaffold dissolution directly to functional myofiber maturation. The entirely cell-free, fully resorbable system creates architectural patterning, temporal staging, and functionally coupled self-termination through a single injectable formulation.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose exploiting carbonic anhydrase IV (CA-IV), a recently identified BBB transcytosis receptor with brain-endothelial-enriched expression, as a novel pathway for systemic delivery of protein therapeutics to the brain. Unlike established RMT targets such as TfR and LRP1, CA-IV exhibits a more CNS-focused expression pattern and has only been explored in the context of AAV gene delivery vectors. We will use AI-driven de novo protein design (RFdiffusion/BindCraft) to engineer compact, high-affinity protein binders that engage the CA-IV ectodomain at epitopes distinct from its catalytic site, then fuse these binders to therapeutic proteins to create modular brain-shuttling conjugates. Region-specific targeting will be achieved by layering a second binding moiety that recognizes regionally enriched endothelial surface markers identified through single-cell transcriptomic atlases of brain vascular heterogeneity. Transcytosis efficiency, brain region selectivity, and preservation of CA-IV enzymatic function will be evaluated in humanized CA-IV knock-in mouse models and human BBB-on-chip systems. This approach opens a fundamentally new, non-TfR/non-LRP1 molecular axis for brain delivery of macromolecular therapeutics with region-selective potential.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a two-stage protein delivery platform that bypasses the conventional BBB by targeting the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier at the choroid plexus, followed by engineered tanycyte-mediated transcytosis for brain region-specific parenchymal delivery. Protein therapeutics will be conjugated to peptide ligands selected by in vivo phage display against choroid plexus epithelial transcytosis receptors, enabling systemic intravenous administration and efficient blood-to-CSF transport. Once in the ventricular CSF, the cargo will bear secondary targeting domains — engineered lipocalin scaffolds — that bind tanycyte-specific surface receptors enriched in circumventricular organs such as the median eminence, subfornical organ, or organum vasculosum of the lamina terminalis, exploiting tanycytic transcytosis to reach hypothalamic and limbic circuits. The approach leverages the anatomical specificity of tanycyte subtypes whose long processes extend into defined neuronal populations. Validation will employ in vivo two-photon imaging and region-specific pharmacodynamic readouts in rodent models. This strategy offers a mechanistically distinct, non-BBB-centric route for region-selective brain protein delivery via systemic administration.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose developing engineered neural-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) displaying computationally designed miniprotein scaffolds that exploit a lipid-composition-mediated transcytosis pathway distinct from classical RMT. Neural-origin EVs possess intrinsic BBB-crossing capacity through membrane-lipid signatures and tetraspanin profiles that facilitate endothelial uptake. We will enhance this by incorporating Mfsd2a-compatible lysophospholipid moieties into the EV membrane, transiently suppressing the transcytosis-inhibitory function of Mfsd2a and promoting caveolae-independent vesicular trafficking across brain endothelium. Protein therapeutics will be loaded into EVs via genetically encoded luminal scaffolds fused to tetraspanin cytoplasmic domains. Brain region specificity will be conferred by surface-displayed de novo designed binders targeting regionally heterogeneous abluminal extracellular matrix components and perivascular cell ligands identified through spatial transcriptomic profiling. This system will be evaluated for region-selective protein delivery using fluorescent reporter cargoes and therapeutic enzyme replacement in murine models of lysosomal storage diseases with CNS involvement.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a synthetic biology approach in which systemically administered brain-endothelial-tropic AAV vectors install a region-specific secretory gene circuit in BBB endothelial cells, converting them into local factories that produce and abluminally secrete the protein therapeutic of interest directly into the brain parenchyma. Region specificity will be achieved through combinatorial regulation: a brain-endothelial-specific minimal promoter (e.g., the recently developed Tek-based miniBEND system) will be intersected with region-enriched cis-regulatory enhancer elements identified from single-cell ATAC-seq data of endothelial cells across nine brain regions. The gene circuit will encode the therapeutic protein fused to a signal peptide directing polarized abluminal secretion. This strategy fundamentally differs from conventional RMT-based delivery because it does not require the protein therapeutic to cross the BBB at all; instead, the genetic instructions cross once via the AAV, and the endothelium continuously manufactures the protein locally. Proof-of-concept will target hippocampal endothelium for sustained local secretion of neurotrophic factors in Alzheimer's disease models.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose harnessing the post-capillary venule perivascular space as a preferential entry corridor for brain delivery by engineering protein-polymer conjugates that exploit adsorptive-mediated transcytosis through a charge-switching mechanism tuned to venular endothelial surface properties. Recent in vivo two-photon studies have shown that post-capillary venules, not capillaries, are the primary sites of nanoparticle brain entry due to their accessible perivascular spaces. We will design pH- and redox-responsive cationic polypeptide shells that encapsulate protein therapeutics: the shell will present a near-neutral surface at systemic pH but transition to a cationic conformation upon encountering the slightly acidic microenvironment of venular endothelial glycocalyx, triggering adsorptive-mediated endocytosis selectively at venules. Brain region selectivity will be introduced by co-grafting peptide aptamers recognizing region-enriched pericyte or astrocyte endfeet markers, which engage after transcytosis in the perivascular space. The system will be validated in mouse models using PET-CT biodistribution and post-mortem immunofluorescent mapping of delivered protein cargo.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a chimeric protein shuttle platform based on computationally redesigned apolipoproteins that hijack the brain's endogenous lipoprotein particle transcytosis machinery — a pathway distinct from classical TfR- or LRP1-mediated RMT. The brain acquires cholesterol and lipoproteins via apolipoprotein E (ApoE) interactions with the VLDL receptor (VLDLR) and ApoER2 (LRP8), which are differentially expressed across brain regions. We will use structure-guided protein engineering to design ApoE-mimetic miniproteins with tunable receptor-selectivity profiles: variants preferring VLDLR will be directed to cerebellar and hippocampal regions where VLDLR is enriched, while ApoER2-preferring variants will target cortical and hippocampal layers. These redesigned shuttle domains will be genetically fused to protein therapeutics, formulated as reconstituted lipoprotein-like nanoparticles, and administered intravenously. Selectivity and brain uptake will be quantified using receptor-knockout mouse panels and spatial proteomics. This approach exploits receptor-subtype selectivity within the lipoprotein receptor family for region-biased brain delivery.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose leveraging the recently characterized molecular heterogeneity of brain endothelial cells across CNS regions to develop a systematic discovery pipeline for region-selective BBB-crossing protein shuttles. Using published and newly generated single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomic datasets from multiple brain regions, we will identify surface-exposed receptors and membrane proteins that are both differentially expressed between regions and competent for transcytosis (based on endosomal trafficking motif analysis and proximity ligation assays). For each validated region-enriched candidate receptor, de novo designed miniprotein binders will be computationally generated, fused to model protein cargoes, and screened in region-specific human iPSC-derived BBB organoid models to assess transcytosis rates. Lead shuttle-cargo fusions will then be evaluated in vivo for region-selective brain accumulation. This platform approach moves beyond single-receptor strategies and provides a generalizable framework for matching protein therapeutics to brain regions via their unique vascular molecular addresses, enabling precision CNS pharmacology.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering bifunctional fusion proteins that exploit the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway's regional heterogeneity at the BBB as a novel non-classical transcytosis mechanism for region-specific brain delivery. Different Wnt ligands (Wnt7a/b in ventral brain, Norrin in retina, Wnt1/3/3a in dorsal brain) pattern BBB formation region-specifically, and key Wnt co-receptors such as Frizzled receptors and LRP5/6 remain differentially expressed in adult brain endothelium. We will design engineered Wnt-mimetic protein domains — truncated, non-signaling variants that retain receptor binding but lack pathway activation — fused to therapeutic protein cargoes. These Wnt-mimetics will engage region-specific Frizzled subtypes to trigger receptor-mediated internalization and transcytosis without perturbing BBB integrity or Wnt signaling homeostasis. Structure-activity relationships will be mapped using cryo-EM-guided mutagenesis and pathway-reporter assays. The approach will be validated in transgenic Wnt-reporter mice for region-selective uptake and in human brain endothelial cell models for transcytosis competence and signaling neutrality.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to therapeutically target adipocyte-derived β2-microglobulin (B2M) to disrupt MHC-I-mediated activation of adipose-resident CD8-positive T cells and ferroptosis-driven macrophage M1 polarization in obesity. While recent work has identified adipocyte B2M as a driver of chronic adipose inflammation, no study has systematically evaluated adipose-targeted B2M silencing in a translational pipeline spanning organ-on-chip and in vivo models. We will engineer an adipocyte-macrophage-T-cell organ-on-chip under lipid-overload conditions to test adeno-associated virus (AAV)-delivered short hairpin RNAs against B2M, measuring T-cell activation, ferroptosis markers, and cytokine output. Parallel experiments in adipocyte-specific B2M-knockout transgenic mice on a high-fat diet will assess systemic inflammation, insulin sensitivity, and immune cell composition via scRNA-seq of the stromal-vascular fraction. By linking human-relevant chip pharmacology to in vivo validation and single-cell resolution of the immune landscape, this work will establish B2M as a druggable node and define the therapeutic window for adipocyte-targeted antigen-presentation blockade in metabolic disease.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to inhibit adipocyte-specific ceramide synthase 6 (CerS6) to reduce C16:0 ceramide accumulation and its downstream pro-inflammatory signaling cascade in obese adipose tissue. Elevated C16:0 ceramide in hypertrophic adipocytes drives mitochondrial fission, TLR4-dependent NF-κB activation, and macrophage recruitment, but CerS6-selective therapeutic strategies have not been evaluated in integrated human-relevant platforms. We will use CRISPR-based CerS6 knockdown in human iPSC-derived adipocytes within a vascularized adipose-on-chip, cocultured with iPSC-derived macrophages, to quantify changes in sphingolipid profiles, cytokine secretion, and macrophage polarization. High-fat-diet-fed CerS6 adipocyte-conditional knockout mice will be profiled by scRNA-seq to map how ceramide depletion reshapes adipocyte-macrophage communication networks and inflammatory gene programs at single-cell resolution. This integrative approach will delineate the causal contribution of adipocyte CerS6-derived ceramides to tissue inflammation and evaluate CerS6 as a precision therapeutic target for obesity-associated metabolic inflammation.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to target the PIEZO1 mechanosensory pathway in hypertrophic adipocytes to interrupt mechano-inflammatory signaling that propagates adipose tissue inflammation during obesity. Adipocyte hypertrophy generates mechanical stress that upregulates PIEZO1, activating NLRP3 inflammasome components and pro-inflammatory cytokine release, yet the therapeutic potential of adipocyte-specific PIEZO1 modulation remains unexplored. We will develop a tunable-stiffness adipose organ-on-chip that replicates the fibrotic extracellular matrix of obese adipose tissue, treating human primary adipocytes and macrophages with PIEZO1 pharmacological modulators (GsMTx4, Yoda1) to dissect mechano-inflammatory coupling. Adipocyte-specific PIEZO1 conditional knockout mice will be challenged with high-fat diet, and visceral adipose tissue will be profiled with snRNA-seq to identify adipocyte subpopulations responsive to mechanical stress and their inflammatory transcriptional signatures. This strategy will determine whether modulating adipocyte mechanosensation can prevent the transition from metabolically healthy to inflamed adipose tissue, defining PIEZO1 as a novel anti-inflammatory target.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to leverage adipocyte-specific senolytic therapy targeting the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) of pre-adipocytes and mature adipocytes to reduce paracrine inflammatory signaling in obese adipose tissue. While senolytics have shown systemic metabolic benefits, no study has combined adipocyte-targeted senolytic delivery with single-cell characterization to resolve which senescent adipocyte subpopulations are the dominant SASP sources. We will encapsulate the senolytic combination dasatinib plus quercetin in adipocyte-homing peptide-conjugated nanoparticles and test them in a human adipose-macrophage organ-on-chip model under chronic lipid overload, quantifying SASP factor output, macrophage polarization, and bystander senescence propagation. In high-fat-diet-fed mice, systemic versus adipose-targeted senolytic delivery will be compared, with snRNA-seq used to map the elimination of specific senescent adipocyte and pre-adipocyte clusters and the resulting shifts in immune cell composition. This work will establish the first adipocyte-resolution map of SASP contributors in obesity and validate targeted senolysis as a precision anti-inflammatory strategy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to intercept adipocyte-derived pro-inflammatory extracellular vesicle (EV) cargo by targeting the neutral sphingomyelinase nSMase2 (SMPD3), which controls EV biogenesis in hypertrophic adipocytes. Obese adipocytes release EVs enriched in pro-inflammatory miRNAs such as miR-34a and miR-155 that drive M1 macrophage polarization, yet therapeutic blockade of adipocyte EV release has not been tested in physiologically relevant models. We will use GW4869 (nSMase2 inhibitor) and CRISPR-mediated SMPD3 deletion in human adipocytes within a microfluidic organ-on-chip system cocultured with primary macrophages, quantifying EV number, miRNA content, and macrophage inflammatory phenotype. Adipocyte-specific SMPD3-knockout mice on high-fat diet will be phenotyped metabolically and their adipose tissue subjected to scRNA-seq to determine how blocking EV release remodels immune cell landscapes and adipocyte-macrophage signaling. This approach addresses a gap in understanding how adipocyte EV biogenesis can be therapeutically modulated to break the inflammatory feed-forward loop between adipocytes and immune cells in obesity.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to attenuate adipocyte-driven inflammation by selectively inhibiting the adipocyte HIF-1α–ANT2 axis, which links mitochondrial uncoupling to hypoxia-induced inflammatory gene expression in expanding adipose tissue. Prior work showed that saturated fatty acids stimulate ANT2-dependent uncoupled respiration in adipocytes, creating relative hypoxia and HIF-1α activation that initiates the chronic inflammatory response, but targeted pharmacological disruption has not been tested in human translational models. We will establish a gradient-oxygenation adipose organ-on-chip with human adipocytes and immune cells to model physiological hypoxia zonation, testing small-molecule ANT2 inhibitors and adipocyte-specific HIF-1α degraders on inflammatory outputs including cytokine release, macrophage chemotaxis, and crown-like structure formation. In parallel, adipocyte-specific HIF-1α conditional knockout mice will undergo high-fat diet challenge followed by snRNA-seq to identify how HIF-1α ablation reshapes adipocyte transcriptional trajectories from adaptive to pathological states. This integrated strategy will define the therapeutic window for targeting hypoxia-inflammatory coupling in distinct adipocyte subpopulations.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to disrupt the pro-inflammatory adipocyte-to-macrophage communication mediated by adipocyte pyroptosis through pharmacological inhibition of NLRP3-caspase-1-GSDMD signaling specifically in adipocytes. Recent evidence shows that pyroptotic, but not apoptotic, adipocytes activate STING and promote TREM2 shedding via ADAM10/17 upregulation in macrophages, driving a dysfunctional macrophage phenotype, yet the therapeutic potential of selectively blocking adipocyte pyroptosis has not been evaluated. We will induce adipocyte pyroptosis with palmitate and LPS in a human iPSC-derived adipocyte-macrophage organ-on-chip and test adipocyte-specific GSDMD-inhibiting strategies, including disulfiram and lipid-nanoparticle-delivered GSDMD siRNA, measuring downstream macrophage STING activation and TREM2 cleavage. Adipocyte-specific GSDMD conditional knockout mice on high-fat diet will be characterized metabolically and by scRNA-seq of adipose tissue to reveal how preventing adipocyte pyroptosis alters macrophage heterogeneity and the balance between lipid-associated macrophages and inflammatory macrophage clusters. This study will establish whether blocking the specific mode of adipocyte cell death can therapeutically redirect macrophage phenotypes to resolve adipose inflammation.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to exploit the recently discovered role of adipocyte glutamine depletion in driving epigenetic pro-inflammatory reprogramming through the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway and O-GlcNAcylation. Reduced glutamine in obese adipocytes increases UDP-GlcNAc production, promoting nuclear O-GlcNAcylation that activates transcription of inflammatory genes, but targeted metabolic rescue via glutamine supplementation or O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) inhibition has not been systematically assessed. We will use an adipose organ-on-chip with human adipocytes under nutrient-excess conditions to test OGT inhibitors and glutamine supplementation, measuring O-GlcNAcylation status, inflammatory gene expression, and macrophage activation in coculture. Adipocyte-specific OGT conditional knockout mice will be placed on high-fat diet and visceral adipose tissue profiled by snRNA-seq to determine how reducing O-GlcNAcylation reprograms the inflammatory transcriptome across adipocyte subpopulations and alters immune cell recruitment. This metabolic-epigenetic approach addresses a novel and druggable adipocyte-intrinsic mechanism of inflammation initiation, distinct from classical cytokine-centric strategies.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose to target adipocyte-specific miR-802 as a novel therapeutic axis that sensitizes NF-κB signaling and establishes a vicious pro-inflammatory cycle between adipocytes and macrophages. Recent evidence demonstrates that miR-802 is upregulated in adipocytes before macrophage infiltration and promotes adipose inflammation through NF-κB pathway sensitization, but therapeutic antisense approaches have not been tested in advanced preclinical models. We will deliver anti-miR-802 locked nucleic acid oligonucleotides to human adipocytes within an adipose-macrophage organ-on-chip under high-palmitate conditions, evaluating NF-κB reporter activity, cytokine secretion, and macrophage migration and polarization dynamics in real time. In adipocyte-specific miR-802 knockout transgenic mice challenged with high-fat diet, we will perform longitudinal snRNA-seq at early and late obesity time points to resolve how miR-802 silencing prevents the inflammatory transcriptional switch in adipocytes and blocks subsequent immune cell infiltration. This work will validate miR-802 as a targetable initiating signal in adipocyte-driven inflammation, potentially enabling RNA-therapeutic intervention before overt metabolic dysfunction develops.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an intra-articular injectable hydrogel system incorporating melatonin-responsive and ROS-responsive dual-gated nanocarriers for pre-emptive drug release in rheumatoid arthritis. The hydrogel matrix contains nanoparticles whose shells are cross-linked by boronate ester bonds (ROS-cleavable) and gated by melatonin-binding aptamers that undergo conformational change upon binding rising nighttime melatonin in the synovial fluid, functioning as an AND-logic gate. Because melatonin levels peak during late night hours and ROS is elevated specifically in inflamed joints, the system releases anti-inflammatory payloads (e.g., dexamethasone or IL-1 receptor antagonist) only when both circadian (high melatonin) and inflammatory (high ROS) conditions coincide, achieving lesion-specific, pre-emptive chronotherapy without external timers. Secondary integration of MMP-cleavable peptide linkers on the nanocarrier surface adds a third layer of specificity that responds to the inflammatory stage of the synovium. Feasibility is supported by existing aptamer-gated mesoporous silica technology, established ROS-responsive boronate chemistry, and the known circadian melatonin gradient in arthritic joints.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We describe a synthetic biology approach using engineered macrophage-lineage cells harboring a dual-input AND-gate gene circuit that couples a circadian E'-box promoter element with an NF-κB response element to produce anti-TNF-α nanobodies in a phase-advanced, inflammation-dependent manner. Unlike existing OR-gate chronogenetic circuits that respond to either input independently, this AND-gate architecture requires simultaneous circadian activation (peaking in the late-night window preceding morning stiffness) and local NF-κB signaling from the inflamed joint microenvironment, ensuring drug output is restricted to diseased tissue at the optimal circadian phase. The macrophages are delivered intra-articularly and engraft within the synovium, using the host's circadian cues to entrain their output timing. A secondary cell-cycle-responsive degradation tag on the nanobody transcript further limits production to actively proliferating inflammatory macrophages, integrating immune activation state with circadian timing. This approach is feasible given demonstrated chronogenetic circuits in iPSC-derived cells and established NF-κB-responsive promoter engineering.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose cortisol-gradient-sensing polymeric nanoparticles that exploit the endogenous circadian nadir of cortisol in arthritic joints to trigger drug release during the pre-dawn window. The nanoparticles are coated with a glucocorticoid receptor ligand-binding domain fusion protein that, in the presence of cortisol, maintains a compact conformation holding the particle shell closed; as cortisol drops to its circadian nadir (approximately 2-4 AM), the protein relaxes, exposing ROS-labile linkers that are cleaved only in the inflamed synovial microenvironment. This dual-sensing mechanism — cortisol-low as a circadian phase sensor and ROS-high as an inflammation sensor — creates an endogenous AND-gate that confines drug release to inflamed joints during the critical pre-flare period. The payload (methotrexate or a JAK inhibitor) is thus delivered preemptively, several hours before morning stiffness peaks. The system is designed for intra-articular depot injection and can be validated using established collagen-induced arthritis models with serial synovial fluid cortisol and cytokine measurements.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We design a DNA nanodevice-gated mesoporous silica nanoparticle platform that integrates sensing of circadian clock protein oscillations and inflammatory cytokines for temporally precise drug release in autoimmune joints. The mesoporous silica pores are capped with DNA origami lids functionalized with two aptamers: one binding REV-ERBα protein (which peaks during the late-night anti-phase of BMAL1 in synoviocytes) and another binding IL-6 (elevated in inflamed joints). When both targets are simultaneously present, a toehold-mediated strand displacement cascade opens the DNA lid, releasing the enclosed anti-inflammatory drug. This AND-logic gate ensures that release occurs only at the intersection of the correct circadian phase (high REV-ERBα, corresponding to late night) and active inflammation (high IL-6), achieving site-specific and time-specific chronotherapy entirely through endogenous signals. The platform is validated using RA synovial fibroblast co-culture systems with clock-synchronized cells, and its translational potential is supported by the established biocompatibility of mesoporous silica and the modularity of DNA aptamer engineering.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an engineered extracellular vesicle system derived from clock-gene-modified mesenchymal stem cells for autonomous circadian drug delivery in autoimmune arthritis. MSCs are transduced with a synthetic gene circuit placing therapeutic cargo (IL-10 or soluble TNF receptor) under a Rev-Erbα response element (RRE) promoter, producing peak secretion of drug-loaded exosomes during the late-night circadian phase. These exosomes are further engineered to display surface folate receptor beta-targeting peptides, restricting uptake to activated macrophages in the inflamed synovium and ensuring lesion specificity. Inflammatory stage integration is achieved by incorporating an IRES-linked NF-κB-dependent amplifier module that boosts therapeutic output proportionally to the degree of local inflammation. The MSCs are implanted in a peri-articular hydrogel depot that entrains to the host light-dark cycle, providing sustained circadian production over weeks. This biologically autonomous system eliminates reliance on external timing, responds dynamically to both circadian and inflammatory inputs, and is feasible using current lentiviral transduction and MSC tissue engineering methods.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a temperature-circadian hybrid nanocarrier system that exploits the endogenous circadian oscillation of joint temperature as the primary sensing axis. Intra-articular temperature in RA joints exhibits measurable circadian variation, with a nadir during late night, superimposed on an inflammatory-stage-dependent elevation above healthy tissue baseline. We design thermoresponsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide)-based nanoparticles with a tuned lower critical solution temperature set to the specific late-night temperature window of inflamed joints (approximately 33-34°C), below which the particles swell and release drug. To ensure inflammation specificity, the nanoparticle shell incorporates MMP-cleavable peptide cross-linkers that must be partially degraded before temperature-triggered swelling can occur; this AND-gate restricts release to MMP-rich arthritic microenvironments during the circadian temperature nadir. The payload is a glucocorticoid pro-drug activated intracellularly by macrophage esterases, adding a third specificity layer for immune-cell targeting. This system senses purely endogenous signals, requires no electronic components, and is implementable with established PNIPAM and MMP-responsive polymer chemistry.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We develop a hypoxia-circadian dual-responsive nanoplatform for autoimmune arthritis that leverages the circadian fluctuation of hypoxia-inducible factor 1α in inflamed synovium. The RA synovial microenvironment exhibits chronic hypoxia due to tissue proliferation exceeding angiogenesis, and HIF-1α expression is further modulated by the circadian clock through BMAL1-mediated transcriptional regulation, peaking during late night. We engineer nitroimidazole-functionalized polymeric nanoparticles that undergo hydrophobic-to-hydrophilic transition and disassemble under hypoxic conditions, releasing encapsulated JAK inhibitors. Crucially, the release threshold is calibrated to the degree of hypoxia achieved only during the late-night HIF-1α peak in inflamed joints, not during baseline daytime hypoxia or in normoxic healthy tissue, thereby creating an endogenous circadian-gated release mechanism. An additional pH-responsive inner core ensures secondary gating at the acidic pH of the inflammatory microenvironment. The system is validated using HIF-reporter synovial fibroblast cultures under circadian entrainment and collagen-induced arthritis models with longitudinal joint oxygen measurements.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a macrophage membrane-coated nanoparticle platform with an internal circadian clock-responsive prodrug activation system for RA chronotherapy. The nanoparticles are coated with activated M1 macrophage membranes, enabling inherent homing to inflamed synovial tissue through native adhesion molecules and chemokine receptors while evading immune clearance. The therapeutic core contains a methotrexate prodrug conjugated via a linker that is cleaved by the circadian-oscillating enzyme DBP (D-site albumin promoter binding protein), whose activity peaks in the late night in synovial cells and is amplified during inflammatory activation. DBP-cleavable peptide linkers function as endogenous circadian timers, releasing active drug preferentially during the pre-dawn hours when DBP peaks. A secondary ROS-responsive shell layer adds lesion specificity by requiring the oxidative microenvironment of inflamed joints for initial shell degradation before the prodrug becomes accessible to DBP. This system integrates circadian enzyme sensing with inflammatory microenvironment gating using clinically translatable biomimetic nanoparticle technology.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We describe a self-regulating hydrogel microsphere system for intra-articular injection that couples adenosine-sensing with circadian and inflammatory inputs for RA drug delivery. Extracellular adenosine in RA joints oscillates with circadian periodicity, rising during nighttime metabolic quiescence, and simultaneously reaches elevated concentrations in hypoxic inflamed tissue due to ATP catabolism. We engineer aptamer-functionalized hydrogel microspheres in which adenosine-binding aptamer crosslinks maintain gel integrity; as adenosine concentration rises past a threshold during the late-night circadian peak in inflamed joints, competitive aptamer-adenosine binding weakens the crosslinks, causing gel swelling and payload release. The threshold is calibrated such that only the combination of circadian-peak adenosine levels and inflammation-elevated baseline adenosine triggers release, constituting an endogenous AND-gate. The microspheres carry dexamethasone-loaded PLGA nanoparticles that provide sustained local release once liberated. This approach leverages established adenosine aptamer technology and PLGA nanoparticle engineering, and can be evaluated in adenosine-reporter transgenic arthritis models.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a topical microneedle patch that delivers a dual-responsive hydrogel depot into keloid tissue, leveraging the coincidence of elevated tissue stiffness and low pH (lactic acidosis) unique to the keloid microenvironment to achieve selective drug release. The hydrogel matrix would be composed of acid-labile acetal-crosslinked polyethylene glycol chains interlaced with stiffness-sensing mechanophore linkers; under the combined conditions of high matrix rigidity (above 20 kPa, characteristic of keloid but not normal dermis) and acidic pH (below 6.8, from keloid glycolytic metabolism), the mechanophore-acetal dual-lock system would unlock and release encapsulated PPARγ-stabilizing small molecules (e.g., a non-thiazolidinedione selective PPARγ modulator) that reinforce the adipocyte transcriptional program and block dedifferentiation. In normal skin, where stiffness and pH remain physiological, neither trigger alone is sufficient for payload release, conferring microenvironment selectivity and preserving normal adipocyte function. A single microneedle application would deposit the slowly eroding depot in the upper-to-mid dermis, providing sustained release over weeks. This AND-gate responsive delivery paradigm, combining mechanical and metabolic discrimination for keloid-selective anti-fibrotic therapy targeting adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition, has not been previously attempted.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose engineering lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles with surfaces decorated by collagen-mimetic peptides that preferentially bind to the highly crosslinked, hydroxylysine-aldehyde-rich collagen matrix distinctive to keloid tissue. Lysyl oxidase-mediated crosslinking produces neo-epitopes (pyridinoline and deoxypyridinoline crosslinks) that are markedly enriched in keloid collagen compared to normal dermal collagen, providing a molecular homing signal. The nanoparticles would encapsulate siRNA targeting the mechanosensitive transcription co-activator YAP, whose nuclear translocation in keloid adipocytes drives their dedifferentiation and transition to a myofibroblast-like state. By tethering cargo release to crosslink-specific ECM anchoring, the nanoparticles accumulate selectively in pathological tissue after topical application via a penetration-enhancing cream base, while being rapidly cleared from normal skin lacking such crosslink density. The slow degradation of the lipid-polymer matrix by keloid-enriched matrix metalloproteinases would ensure weeks-long sustained siYAP release from a single application. This ECM-crosslink-targeted topical nanomedicine approach for blocking adipocyte dedifferentiation in keloids is unprecedented.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a topical, oxygen-consuming enzymatic hydrogel patch that exploits the intrinsic hypoxia vulnerability of keloid tissue to selectively protect adipocytes from dedifferentiation. The formulation contains glucose oxidase embedded in a mucoadhesive hydrogel applied over keloid lesions; by catalytically consuming residual oxygen at the tissue surface, the patch deepens local hypoxia specifically in the already oxygen-starved keloid microenvironment to a threshold that triggers adipocyte-autonomous survival through HIF-2α-mediated upregulation of PPARγ and adiponectin, paradoxically stabilizing the adipocyte phenotype against TGF-β-driven dedifferentiation. Critically, in normal adjacent skin where baseline oxygenation is adequate, the modest surface oxygen reduction has negligible biological effect due to compensatory vascular perfusion. Co-loaded into the patch are controlled-release microspheres of a lactate dehydrogenase inhibitor that interrupts the lactate-H3K18 lactylation-TGF-β1 positive feedback loop driving fibroblast activation exclusively in the glycolytically active keloid. Single application of the patch maintains enzymatic activity for several weeks through stabilized enzyme depots. This metabolic-reprogramming topical strategy targeting the keloid's unique metabolic vulnerability to protect adipocyte identity is entirely novel.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a dissolving microneedle array that implants mechanosensitive hydrogel microbeads into keloid tissue, where the elevated matrix stiffness (typically 20–100 kPa versus 2–5 kPa in normal skin) serves as the sole trigger for sustained therapeutic release. The microbeads are fabricated from alginate crosslinked with short, tension-sensitive DNA duplex nanoswitches: when embedded in stiff keloid ECM, cellular contractile forces transmitted through integrin-mediated adhesion mechanically unzip the DNA crosslinks, progressively opening the microbead pores to release encapsulated GsMTx4, a Piezo1 channel inhibitor peptide. In the compliant environment of normal skin, insufficient mechanical force preserves microbead integrity, preventing drug release and thereby protecting normal adipocyte function. Released GsMTx4 blocks Piezo1-mediated mechanotransduction in keloid adipocytes, preventing YAP nuclear translocation and the adipocyte-to-fibroblast transition that fuels keloid fibrosis. The DNA-crosslinked architecture provides tunable stiffness thresholds and multi-week release kinetics from a single administration. This stiffness-gated, mechanically triggered topical delivery of Piezo inhibitors to selectively block adipocyte dedifferentiation within keloid tissue represents a novel convergence of DNA nanotechnology and anti-fibrotic therapy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a topical lipid nanoparticle formulation delivering adipocyte-lineage-restricted epigenetic editing cargo to keloid tissue, leveraging the keloid's uniquely enriched mast cell-derived histamine and tryptase as microenvironment-selective activation signals. The lipid nanoparticles carry CRISPR-dCas9-TET1 mRNA together with guide RNAs targeting the hypermethylated PPARγ and ADIPOQ promoter regions in keloid-resident dedifferentiating adipocytes, aiming to demethylate and reactivate adipogenic gene programs. The nanoparticle surface incorporates protease-activated cell-penetrating peptides that are unmasked exclusively by keloid-enriched tryptase, enabling selective cellular uptake in the keloid immune microenvironment while remaining inert on normal skin. A microneedle-assisted single topical application deposits the formulation intradermally, where the mast cell protease-rich milieu activates uptake and the epigenetic editing cargo provides durable re-expression of adipocyte identity genes without requiring repeated dosing. This approach uniquely integrates immune-microenvironment-triggered delivery with epigenetic reprogramming to restore adipocyte identity, an angle that has not been explored for keloid therapy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a topical biomimetic vesicle system derived from normal dermal adipocyte membranes, loaded with a sustained-release pro-adipogenic cocktail, and functionalized with ROS-cleavable stealth coatings that are selectively stripped in the oxidative keloid microenvironment. Normal skin adipocytes express PD-L1 and other surface markers that facilitate immunological tolerance and paracrine signaling; by engineering vesicles from their membranes, the platform inherits homing affinity for adipocyte-lineage cells undergoing dedifferentiation in keloids while minimizing immune clearance. The ROS-responsive poly(propylene sulfide) coating remains intact in normoxic, low-ROS normal skin but is oxidized and shed in keloid tissue, which exhibits elevated mitochondrial and NADPH-oxidase-derived ROS, thereby exposing the adipocyte membrane ligands for targeted fusion with transitioning cells. The vesicle cargo includes BMP4 and a PPARγ-stabilizing peptidomimetic that synergistically redirect dedifferentiating adipocytes back toward a mature phenotype while antagonizing TGF-β-driven myofibroblast commitment. A single cream-based application with skin-penetration enhancers achieves depot-like release from the biomimetic vesicle reservoir over weeks. This adipocyte-membrane-biomimetic, ROS-gated approach for keloid-specific adipocyte rescue is unprecedented.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an injectable topical microcrystalline depot formulation of a dual MCT1/LOXL2 inhibitor prodrug designed to be activated only within the acidic, lactate-rich, mechanically stiff keloid microenvironment. The prodrug is a chimeric molecule linking an MCT1 inhibitor moiety (blocking lactate-driven histone lactylation that promotes adipocyte dedifferentiation and fibroblast activation) to a LOXL2 inhibitor moiety (preventing collagen crosslinking and tissue stiffening) via an acid-labile ester bond that hydrolyzes preferentially at the low pH characteristic of keloid tissue. Applied topically through a microneedle-assisted cream, the crystalline depot slowly dissolves over weeks, releasing intact prodrug that remains inactive at the neutral pH of normal skin. Upon activation in keloid tissue, the dual inhibitor simultaneously interrupts the lactate-fibrosis positive feedback loop and the stiffness-mechanotransduction cycle that together drive adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition. By targeting two mechanistically distinct but synergistic pathological axes through a single pH-gated prodrug, this strategy provides keloid selectivity while preserving normal adipocyte metabolism and is a previously unattempted therapeutic concept.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a topical hydrogel containing engineered extracellular vesicles loaded with miR-30a mimics and coated with mechanosensitive liposomal shells that rupture under high compressive stress, releasing their cargo specifically within the high-tension keloid microenvironment. MiR-30a is a potent positive regulator of adipogenesis through PPARγ stabilization and a negative regulator of the TGF-β/Smad axis, making it uniquely positioned to simultaneously maintain adipocyte identity and block myofibroblast transition. The mechanosensitive liposomal shell is composed of a fluid-phase lipid bilayer incorporating cholesterol-poor domains that undergo phase transition and rupture when subjected to the sustained compressive forces (above a threshold of approximately 5 kPa) generated by the dense, contracted keloid ECM. In normal skin, where interstitial pressure and ECM compressive forces are far lower, the vesicles remain intact and are eventually cleared without cargo release, ensuring selectivity. A hyaluronic acid-based hydrogel carrier applied topically provides both skin adhesion and slow diffusion of vesicles into the dermis, enabling sustained effect from a single application. This mechanically gated miRNA delivery strategy targeting adipocyte phenotype preservation in keloids is entirely novel.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a multi-component allogeneic HSCT platform that replaces genotoxic conditioning with a dual antibody-based regimen targeting CD117 (c-Kit) via an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) to selectively deplete host hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, combined with anti-CD47 blocking antibody to simultaneously strip the anti-phagocytic shield from leukemia stem cells and enhance their macrophage-mediated clearance. To dislodge niche-sequestered LSCs, peri-conditioning CXCR4 antagonism (e.g., plerixafor or BL-8040) would be administered to mobilize quiescent LSCs from protective bone marrow niches into the circulation, where they become susceptible to antibody-mediated elimination and subsequent donor immune surveillance. Post-engraftment GVL augmentation without exacerbated GVHD would be achieved through infusion of donor-derived memory T cells (CD45RA-depleted graft) and ex vivo expanded donor regulatory T cells at a defined Treg:Tcon ratio, leveraging the observation that memory T cells mediate potent GVL while having minimal GVHD-inducing capacity. This integrated strategy compensates for the absence of myeloablative cytoreduction by layering selective HSC depletion, LSC-targeted immune opsonization, niche disruption, and calibrated adoptive immunotherapy, with the hypothesis that relapse rates will match or improve upon those achieved by conventional MAC.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a non-genotoxic conditioning and post-transplant immunotherapy strategy in which PARP inhibitor pre-treatment is used before and continued briefly after allogeneic HSCT to epigenetically upregulate NKG2D ligands (MICA/B, ULBPs) on NKG2D-ligand-negative leukemia stem cells, thereby unmasking them for NK-cell-mediated killing. Conditioning combines a CD117-ADC for selective host HSC depletion with a JAK1/2 inhibitor (ruxolitinib) to suppress host T- and NK-cell-mediated graft rejection without broad genotoxicity, as recently demonstrated in preclinical fully-mismatched allogeneic models. Post-engraftment, the donor graft is engineered as a CD45RA-depleted product enriched for memory T cells and supplemented with IL-15-activated donor NK cells to maximize GVL while minimizing naive-T-cell-driven GVHD. Simultaneous anti-CD47 antibody administration enhances macrophage phagocytosis of residual LSCs while paradoxically mitigating GVHD by promoting clearance of alloreactive donor T cells that upregulate CD47 upon activation. This multi-pronged approach addresses LSC immune evasion through NKG2DL restoration, CD47 blockade, and NK-cell activation, while preserving GVL-GVHD separation through graft engineering and JAK inhibition.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a sequential transplant platform in which pre-transplant venetoclax plus azacitidine bridge therapy is used not merely for cytoreduction but specifically to prime LSCs for immune-mediated elimination by disrupting their metabolic dependence on oxidative phosphorylation and shifting their BCL-2/MCL-1 apoptotic balance, thereby increasing their vulnerability to subsequent donor immune attack. Non-genotoxic conditioning consists of anti-CD117-ADC for host HSC niche clearance combined with fludarabine at reduced doses sufficient for immunosuppression but below myeloablative thresholds, paired with CXCR4 antagonist infusion to mobilize residual niche-anchored LSCs. Post-transplant maintenance employs a bispecific antibody engaging CD3 on donor T cells and CD123 on LSCs, providing targeted GVL effect against the LSC compartment without broadly activating alloreactive T cells against normal tissues. GVHD prophylaxis utilizes post-transplant cyclophosphamide, which preferentially preserves regulatory T cells via their high aldehyde dehydrogenase activity while eliminating rapidly proliferating alloreactive conventional T cells. This design compensates for the reduced cytotoxic intensity of conditioning by integrating LSC metabolic priming, targeted niche disruption, and precision post-transplant immunotherapy.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a strategy that combines antibody-mediated non-genotoxic conditioning with a genetically engineered donor NK-cell product designed to overcome the multi-layered immune evasion of leukemia stem cells. Conditioning uses anti-CD45 radioimmunconjugate at targeted doses sufficient for HSC niche depletion but below systemic genotoxic thresholds, delivered via pretargeted radioimmunotherapy with a bispecific antibody-streptavidin construct followed by a radiolabeled biotin chase, thereby concentrating radiation specifically to the bone marrow. The donor cellular product comprises CRISPR-edited allogeneic NK cells bearing an NKG2D-chimeric antigen receptor for enhanced recognition of NKG2DL-dim LSCs, with concurrent knockout of the CISH checkpoint gene to sustain NK-cell cytotoxicity in the immunosuppressive bone marrow microenvironment. Hypomethylating agent maintenance (decitabine) is administered post-engraftment to simultaneously upregulate NKG2D ligands on residual LSCs and enhance HLA class II expression, boosting both innate and adaptive donor immune recognition. This approach addresses sanctuary niche protection via marrow-targeted radiation, overcomes the NKG2DL-negative phenotype of LSCs through both pharmacological upregulation and receptor engineering, and preserves GVL while limiting GVHD through the use of NK cells rather than unselected T cells as the primary effector population.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a novel post-transplant consolidation strategy based on donor-derived invariant NKT (iNKT) cells engineered to express a chimeric antigen receptor targeting CD33, combined with peri-transplant niche disruption and multi-checkpoint blockade, within a non-genotoxic conditioning framework. The conditioning backbone uses anti-CD117 plus anti-CD47 blocking antibodies with JAK1/2 inhibition to achieve toxic-payload-free host HSC depletion and donor engraftment across HLA barriers, as validated in recent preclinical models achieving greater than 80 percent donor chimerism. iNKT-CAR33 cells exploit the unique biology of iNKT cells, which mediate potent anti-tumor cytotoxicity and regulate inflammatory responses through their invariant TCR-CD1d interaction, thus providing GVL without inducing classical TCR-MHC-driven GVHD. To address LSC sanctuary, E-selectin antagonist (uproleselan) is co-administered to disrupt CXCL12-independent adhesive interactions between LSCs and endosteal niche endothelium, complementing CXCR4 blockade for comprehensive mobilization. Post-transplant anti-PD-1 antibody is given at low doses titrated to enhance iNKT and donor NK effector function against PD-L1-expressing LSCs without exacerbating GVHD, enabled by the Treg-preserving effect of the post-transplant cyclophosphamide prophylaxis backbone.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose an integrated transplant platform that employs a bispecific T-cell engager bridging donor T cells to LSC-associated antigens as a pharmacologically controllable substitute for the anti-leukemia effect lost by eliminating myeloablative conditioning. Non-genotoxic conditioning is achieved with an anti-CD117-ADC bearing a tubulin-inhibitor payload to selectively clear host HSPCs while sparing non-hematopoietic tissues, combined with lymphodepleting fludarabine. To overcome the bone marrow niche sanctuary, peri-transplant treatment with a combined CXCR4 antagonist and VLA-4 inhibitor (natalizumab) disrupts both chemokine-mediated and integrin-mediated LSC retention, forcing quiescent LSCs into cell cycle and out of protective niches. The GVL-without-GVHD strategy uses a split-dose graft: first infusion of T-cell-depleted CD34-selected stem cells for engraftment, followed by delayed add-back of donor T cells co-administered with a CD3xCD123 bispecific engager that preferentially directs T-cell cytotoxicity against CD123-high LSCs rather than normal tissues. Anti-CD47 antibody maintenance is layered to block the anti-phagocytic signal on residual LSCs, engaging donor-derived macrophages for innate immune clearance and thereby creating redundant innate and adaptive anti-LSC immune surveillance.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose exploiting the differential epigenetic vulnerability of LSCs versus normal HSCs by using a transient, pre-transplant combination of LSD1 (KDM1A) inhibitor and HDAC inhibitor to force differentiation and surface antigen remodeling of quiescent LSCs without damaging normal HSCs, which lack the aberrant epigenetic dependencies characteristic of leukemic stem cells. This epigenetic priming restores expression of NKG2D ligands, upregulates HLA class I and II molecules, and reduces CD47 surface expression on LSCs, thereby simultaneously addressing multiple immune-evasion mechanisms. Non-genotoxic conditioning with anti-CD117-ADC clears the host HSC niche for donor engraftment, while CXCR4 antagonism mobilizes epigenetically primed LSCs from the bone marrow niche. The donor graft includes both conventional hematopoietic stem cells and a defined dose of ex vivo expanded donor NK cells, which serve as the primary GVL effectors against the now-immunovisible LSCs while avoiding the alloreactivity against epithelial tissues that drives GVHD. This strategy converts LSCs from an immune-invisible, niche-protected state into differentiated, antigen-presenting targets that are highly susceptible to innate immune clearance.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a donor-derived gamma-delta T-cell-based allogeneic HSCT platform that leverages the intrinsic MHC-unrestricted tumor recognition capacity of gamma-delta T cells to provide potent GVL independent of HLA matching, thereby circumventing LSC immune evasion through HLA downregulation. Non-genotoxic conditioning combines anti-CD117-ADC with short-course baricitinib (JAK1/2 inhibitor) for selective niche clearance and host immune suppression, avoiding systemic DNA damage. The donor graft is separated into a CD34-selected HSC fraction for engraftment and an expanded Vdelta1 gamma-delta T-cell product that recognizes stress-induced ligands on LSCs via NKG2D and TCR-mediated pathways independent of classical HLA presentation, making them effective against HLA-loss variants. Pre-transplant niche disruption via combined CXCR4 antagonism and E-selectin blockade dislodges quiescent LSCs, and post-transplant low-dose azacitidine maintenance upregulates NKG2D ligands and tumor-associated antigens on residual LSCs while promoting gamma-delta T-cell persistence. Since gamma-delta T cells do not recognize alloantigens through classical MHC restriction, GVHD risk is intrinsically minimized, and anti-CD47 blockade is added post-engraftment to complement T-cell killing with enhanced macrophage phagocytosis of LSCs.

label: claude_opus_46
text: We propose a closed-loop adaptive immunotherapy approach embedded within a non-genotoxic transplant framework, in which real-time measurable residual disease monitoring by next-generation sequencing guides iterative post-transplant interventions that collectively replace the anti-leukemia effect of myeloablative conditioning. The conditioning backbone uses anti-CD117-ADC plus low-dose fludarabine for selective HSC depletion and immunosuppression, with concurrent CXCR4 antagonist pulses to mobilize niche-sequestered LSCs. Post-engraftment, an adaptive algorithm triggers sequential interventions based on MRD kinetics: first-line response employs donor lymphocyte infusion enriched for leukemia-reactive memory T cells identified by minor histocompatibility antigen screening; second-line response deploys anti-CD47 plus anti-TIM-3 bispecific antibody to simultaneously block the two dominant immune checkpoints on LSCs; and third-line response administers donor-derived CAR-NK cells targeting CLL-1, an antigen preferentially expressed on LSCs but not normal HSCs. GVHD is managed throughout by post-transplant cyclophosphamide followed by sirolimus-based maintenance, which promotes Treg homeostasis while permitting effector responses against leukemia-specific antigens. This MRD-driven, multi-modality approach provides layered defense against relapse without relying on front-loaded genotoxic intensity.

label: claude_opus_46
text: This study proposes a proof-of-concept experiment using primary human keratinocyte-derived epidermal organoids to test whether the order and duration of exposure to S. aureus versus S. epidermidis conditioned media (bacterial cocktails containing secreted metabolites, toxins, and signaling molecules) imprints distinct inflammatory and differentiation states on skin stem cells. Organoids will be subjected to four sequential treatment arms over six weeks: long-term S. aureus cocktail followed by short-term S. epidermidis cocktail, the reverse sequence, simultaneous co-exposure, and untreated controls. Inflammatory status will be assessed by multiplex cytokine profiling (IL-6, IL-8, TSLP, IL-10) and NF-κB/STAT3 pathway activation via western blot, while differentiation capacity will be quantified through clonogenic (holoclone/meroclone/paraclone) assays and expression of stemness markers (p63, K14, K15) versus differentiation markers (K10, involucrin, loricrin) by RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence. This design will determine whether pathobiont-first exposure creates a pro-inflammatory epigenetic priming that commensal signals can reverse, or conversely whether commensal pre-conditioning confers protective tolerance against subsequent pathobiont challenge, directly testing the concept of microbial-order-dependent epithelial stem cell plasticity in a human skin organoid system.

label: claude_opus_46
text: This idea employs bacterial-derived membrane vesicles (MVs) isolated from S. aureus and S. epidermidis as the treatment modality to investigate time-differential imprinting of skin stem cell fate in 3D epidermal organoids. Extracellular vesicles will be purified from planktonic cultures of each species by ultracentrifugation and characterized by nanoparticle tracking analysis and proteomics, then applied to human epidermal organoids in a sequential regimen: 14 days of S. aureus MVs followed by 7 days of S. epidermidis MVs, the inverse order, each species alone, and vehicle controls. Readouts will include ATAC-seq on sorted basal (integrin-α6-high) stem cells to assess chromatin accessibility changes at inflammatory and differentiation gene loci, paired with targeted gene expression panels for trained immunity markers (AIM2, IL-1β, TNF-α) and barrier differentiation genes (FLG, LOR, TGM1). Colony-forming efficiency assays after organoid dissociation will quantify residual stemness. This approach uniquely leverages the cargo-delivery properties of bacterial MVs as physiologically relevant signaling vehicles, enabling mechanistic dissection of how vesicle-encapsulated virulence factors versus commensal-derived immunomodulatory proteins differentially reprogram epidermal stem cell chromatin and functional identity.

label: claude_opus_46
text: This proposal tests the hypothesis that prolonged S. epidermidis-derived signal exposure establishes an aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR)-dependent tolerogenic state in skin organoid stem cells that buffers against subsequent S. aureus-induced inflammatory activation and aberrant differentiation. Human epidermal equivalents generated from primary keratinocytes at the air-liquid interface will be pre-treated with S. epidermidis conditioned medium for 14 days, followed by acute S. aureus conditioned medium challenge for 48 hours, with parallel arms receiving AHR inhibitor (CH-223191) or vehicle during the commensal pre-conditioning phase. Inflammatory status will be measured by LEGENDplex cytokine arrays and RT-qPCR for AHR target genes (CYP1A1, CYP1B1, IL1RA, TNFAIP3), antimicrobial peptide expression (HBD3, RNase7), and barrier integrity markers. Differentiation capacity will be assessed by histological analysis of epidermal stratification, proliferation index (Ki67), and expression of basal versus suprabasal keratins. This mechanistically focused design addresses the gap in understanding whether commensal-derived tryptophan metabolites delivered through conditioned media can establish durable AHR-mediated protection in epidermal progenitors, offering a druggable pathway for therapeutic microbiome modulation in inflammatory skin disease.

label: claude_opus_46
text: This study introduces a dose-escalation temporal framework using bacterial lysate cocktails to model dysbiosis-to-homeostasis and homeostasis-to-dysbiosis transitions in keratinocyte-derived skin organoids, assessing how graded temporal shifts in the S. aureus-to-S. epidermidis signal ratio affect stem cell inflammatory programming and lineage commitment. Organoids will receive bacterial lysates over eight weeks in three treatment trajectories: a progressive shift from high S. aureus to high S. epidermidis ratio (dysbiosis resolution), the reverse trajectory (dysbiosis onset), and a constant equimolar mixture. At biweekly intervals, organoids will be sampled for inflammatory transcriptomics via a focused NanoString nCounter panel covering 50 innate immune and differentiation genes, alongside flow cytometric quantification of basal stem cell markers (integrin-β1, CD49f, EGFR) and differentiation markers (involucrin, transglutaminase-1). Post-treatment clonogenic assays will evaluate long-term regenerative potential. This gradient approach uniquely models the temporal dynamics of microbiome community transitions rather than binary switches, providing quantitative thresholds at which pathobiont signal dominance irreversibly alters stem cell identity versus conditions permitting recovery by commensal signal restoration.

label: claude_opus_46
text: This proposal examines whether S. aureus exosome-mediated inflammatory memory in epidermal stem cells can be erased by subsequent S. epidermidis exosome treatment, using a rest-and-recall experimental paradigm adapted from trained immunity studies. Human epidermal organoids will first receive S. aureus-derived MVs for seven days to establish inflammatory priming, followed by a seven-day washout period without bacterial signals, and then a second challenge with either S. epidermidis MVs, S. aureus MVs, or vehicle for seven days. Inflammatory recall will be measured by comparing secondary cytokine responses (IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α) to primary responses, with single-cell RNA sequencing performed on organoid-derived basal cells at each transition point to capture heterogeneity in inflammatory and stemness gene modules. Chromatin immunoprecipitation for H3K4me1 and H3K27ac at key inflammatory loci (IL6, CXCL8, DEFB4) will evaluate whether commensal vesicles can reset the epigenetic marks deposited by pathobiont priming. This rest-and-recall design directly tests whether microbial-signal-dependent trained immunity in epithelial stem cells is reversible, addressing a fundamental question in skin barrier biology with implications for bacteriotherapy strategies in atopic dermatitis.

label: claude_opus_46
text: This study proposes using a split-organoid paired design in which individual skin organoids are bisected, with each half receiving the reciprocal treatment sequence, to control for inter-organoid variability when assessing how treatment order affects stem cell plasticity. One half of each organoid will receive S. aureus conditioned medium for 14 days followed by S. epidermidis conditioned medium for 7 days, while the matched half receives the inverse sequence. Inflammatory status will be assessed through secreted cytokine kinetics measured every 48 hours by multiplex ELISA, allowing construction of time-resolved inflammatory trajectories for each treatment arm within the same genetic background. At endpoint, organoid halves will be dissociated for paired comparison of colony-forming efficiency, holoclone frequency, and expression of stemness (TP63, ITGA6) versus terminal differentiation markers (IVL, FLG) by RT-qPCR. This internally controlled paired design substantially increases statistical power at POC scale, requiring fewer total organoids while enabling robust detection of order-dependent effects on the inflammatory-to-regenerative axis, a design innovation that addresses a critical limitation of current organoid-based microbiome studies.

label: claude_opus_46
text: This proposal investigates whether bacterial-derived exosome-mediated signaling differentially reprograms the metabolic state of skin organoid stem cells, linking metabolic rewiring to inflammatory and differentiation outcomes. Skin organoids will be treated sequentially with S. aureus MVs (10 days) followed by S. epidermidis MVs (7 days), the reverse order, or single-species controls. At endpoint, basal stem cells will be isolated by FACS (CD49f-high/CD71-low) and subjected to Seahorse metabolic flux analysis measuring oxidative phosphorylation and glycolysis rates, alongside targeted metabolomics profiling of the tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates succinate, fumarate, and alpha-ketoglutarate, known epigenetic-modifying metabolites. Inflammatory cytokine secretion and differentiation marker expression will be correlated with metabolic profiles to establish whether S. aureus signals enforce a glycolytic, pro-inflammatory stem cell state while S. epidermidis signals restore oxidative metabolism and support normal differentiation. This metabolo-epigenetic framework connects bacterial signal sequence to stem cell metabolic reprogramming, offering a mechanistic layer beyond transcriptional profiling and providing candidate metabolic targets for reversing pathobiont-induced stem cell dysfunction.

label: claude_opus_46
text: This study addresses the role of bacterial signal exposure duration thresholds in determining reversibility of stem cell inflammatory priming by systematically varying S. aureus conditioned medium treatment length before applying a fixed S. epidermidis rescue protocol. Human 3D epidermal equivalents will be exposed to S. aureus conditioned medium for 3, 7, 14, or 21 days, each followed by a standardized 7-day S. epidermidis conditioned medium treatment.
